result.description: Fires on verb stems like ampl-, simpl-, intens-, fort-, clar-, ident- where the word continues with the suffix "-ify" (ifies, ifying, ification). Its output pushes those suffix tokens next.
result.label: Stem before -ify suffix

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece 'ogn' (as in "cognition", "cognitive"), plus other word-start fragments like 'ca', 'ag', ' capac', ' pract', ' virt' that need a completion such as "-ition" or "-itive". Peaks on 'ogn' appearing at the start of a sentence or after a break.
result.label: 'ogn' cognition word-piece

result.description: Fires mostly on the piece 'ole' inside "intermolecular" (predicting "cular"), with weaker hits on other word pieces and digits. It stays silent on 'ole' in "Molecular" at the start of a sentence.
result.label: 'ole' in intermolecular

result.description: Fires on the piece ' as' when it begins the word "asserts"/"asserting" (split as 'as'+'ser'), predicting 'ser' continuation. It stays quiet on ' as' used as a standalone conjunction or preposition ("as it states", "such as").
result.label: ' as' starting 'assert' word

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'FE' piece in the acronym "Finite Element Analysis (FEA)", just after the opening parenthesis. A few weaker peaks fall on function words and punctuation. Members detect capital-letter acronym pieces.
result.label: FE in FEA acronym

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' to', ' can', 'ity', commas, ' these', ' and') in technical expository text, mid-phrase. Peaks are mixed and the contrast shows the same ' to' staying silent, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on ' dynamic' used attributively after "the" (e.g. "underscores the dynamic nature of language"), predicting abstract nouns like nature/interplay. Silent on predicative "language is dynamic". Weak activity on other adjective-like words.
result.label: "the dynamic" before abstract noun

result.description: Fires mainly on " of" right after a heading-like word such as "Adverbs of" (manner/time) in grammar-lesson lists. Silent on ordinary "of" in narrative or descriptive prose. Weak activity elsewhere on commas and "the".
result.label: "Adverbs of" grammar heading

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' II' in "Type II error", 'su' in "well-suited", an apostrophe, ' are') in technical or scientific explanatory text, especially statistics. No single token dominates; the circuit is diffuse and weakly faithful.
result.label: Diffuse technical-text mid-phrase tokens

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and modifiers (' inner', ' and', ' that', ' the', ' internal') in the middle of a noun phrase, where an adjective like "inner/large/living" could come next. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is diffuse.
result.label: Scattered function words before adjective

result.description: Fires on creation verbs like " creating", " create", " building" (sometimes " a" after them) in branding and marketing text, where the next word is likely an abstract brand-related object such as an experience, emotion or community. Silent in a CRM software context.
result.label: creating/building verbs in marketing text

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (possessive 's, for, the, of, and, a, an) in expository prose, mid-phrase where a noun or content word is expected next. No single token dominates; the members are mostly generic function-word detectors. Evidence is weak.
result.label: Scattered function words before content

result.description: Fires on prepositions or connectives (among, between, of, from, by) after nouns of concern, conflict or power in historical/geopolitical text about nations and powers. It predicts country or military-diplomatic terms next. Peak tokens are mixed.
result.label: Prepositions in geopolitical history text

result.description: Fires on relative pronouns ' that'/' which' introducing a relative clause after a noun like "earlier approaches", "static models", "early methods", where the clause describes older or contrasting ideas. Silent on many other relative 'that' cases.
result.label: Relative that/which after older approaches

result.description: Fires on the word-piece "co" (mostly " co") when it begins a longer word such as cooperative, coating, cocktail or coaching. It pushes toward continuations like "operation", "aching", "ck", "pper".
result.label: "co" word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' comp' when it begins a longer word, peaking where the continuation is "licate/licating" (complicate). It also fires weakly on other comp- words like compelling and composting. Silent on the whole word "complex".
result.label: ' comp' predicting 'licate'

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (periods ending short list-like headings, ' the', ' directly', ' a', word fragments) with no clear pattern. Logits push toward words like quarter, wave, lake, micro, macro. Peak consistency is low and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered function-word and period peaks

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'comp' piece after the prefix 'un-' (uncomplicated), and also on list commas and connectives (',', ' and', ' between', ' various') in enumerations of academic topics. Mixed; the 'un-' word-piece part is the clearest.
result.label: un-'comp' pieces and list commas

result.description: Fires on the verb "change" and its forms (changes, changing, adjust, alter) when used as a transitive or active verb, often with a following object like color, direction, or perspective. Mostly in language, grammar, or descriptive text.
result.label: Change verb forms

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' expl' when it begins the verb "explored" (passive "will be explored", "are explored"). It is quieter before "-oring" or "-oration" in noun or participle uses.
result.label: ' expl' starting "explored"

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (and, of, from, such, both, -abling) mid-phrase in academic text, where a continuation is expected. Peaks are inconsistent, with no dominant token. The logits are weak and mixed, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered function words in academic prose

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' sust' when it begins "sustainable", especially after adverbs like "ecologically" or "environmentally" or after "more". It is silent on "sustainability" and "sustains" in some contexts.
result.label: ' sust' in "sustainable"

result.description: Fires on a linking verb (' was', 's' in it's, ' is', ' were') right after a subject like "it", "files", "lunch", where an adverb or predicate comes next. Silent when 'was' follows a bare noun in a different construction.
result.label: Copula after subject (was/is/'s)

result.description: Fires on function or verb words like "using", "the", "of", "use" in writing-advice text about sentence structure, active/passive voice and sentence variety, where the next word starts a technique or device. Silent on "using" in other contexts.
result.label: Writing-style advice connector words

result.description: Fires on ' to' (also ' can', ' quickly') right after a technical subject like a system or vehicle, where a verb of function or purpose comes next ("designed to", "allows them to", "vehicles can"). Silent on ' to' as a preposition ("similar to", "from X to Y").
result.label: Infinitive 'to'/'can' before function verb

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' connect' in "connective(s)" in logic text, and on 'ud' in "Plum Pudding" model. Mid-word pieces that need a continuation like "-ives" or "-ding"; mostly logical connectives context.
result.label: connect(ives) and Pud(ding) word pieces

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' man' when it starts a longer word, as in "manometers", "maneuvers" or "managing". It also fires weakly on standalone "man". Members mostly detect ' man' and boost continuations like "aging", "eu" and "made".
result.label: ' man' as word-start piece

result.description: Fires on ' work' and related word pieces (working, brainstorm-ing, cook-ing, coffee) when they come as a modifier or compound inside workplace/social-setting text, e.g. "in work|place", "remote working". Silent on some other ' work' uses like "workforce" or "work and".
result.label: work/workplace compound modifier

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (comma, "of", "the", "as", "to", " z") in abstract academic prose, mid-clause where a verb or noun phrase is expected next. Logits weakly favor "converting/composed". Peaks are inconsistent and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words in academic prose

result.description: Fires on ' War' in "World War I/II" when it is the bare "World War" phrase, mostly after "World". It stays quiet on "the First/Second World War" and other wars (Russo-Japanese War), where the numeral is not expected next.
result.label: World War before numeral

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verb pieces (of, to, by, transmitting, chemical) in science text about biological signaling, cells and processes, where a verb or relation is about to take a mechanism or process object. Weak and mixed evidence.
result.label: Biological signaling connector words

result.description: Fires on the word piece " rh" when it begins "rhythm" (rhythms, rhythmic), predicting continuations like "yth"/"ythm". It was silent on one text-initial " rh" with no preceding context.
result.label: " rh" start of rhythm

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' a', ' same', ' and', ' of') in abstract philosophy-of-mind passages, such as the zombie argument and dualism. It fires where a noun phrase about consciousness or physicalism is about to continue. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words in philosophy of mind

result.description: Fires on " into" (also " an") when plaintext or readable data is being transformed or converted into ciphertext, in encryption text. Silent on "into" in other uses such as "taking into account" or "transformed it into".
result.label: Encryption: plaintext into ciphertext

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and commas (',', ' the', ' by', '),') in texts about disasters, environmental incidents and responses, where a verb or subject is expected next. Peaks are mixed and weak; logits hint at 'pres/sust/consumption'.
result.label: Commas/function words in disaster-response text

result.description: Fires on the 'ed' piece inside the word Veda/Vedanta/Vedic (also on 'Liter' in a list of literary topics, and a few other word-start pieces). Silent on 'ed' as a verb suffix or in other words like feedback.
result.label: 'ed' in Vedic words

result.description: Fires on ' by' (also ' to', ' from', ' of') right after a passive or causal verb like "driven", "shaped", "influenced", "due to", introducing the causes or factors behind language or social change. Silent on agentive "by" meaning "through doing".
result.label: Causal 'by' after shaped/driven

result.description: Fires mainly on the word piece " cub" in "cubic" (face-centered cubic, simple cubic crystal structures), with a few weaker hits on "fr" in refrigeration and other scattered tokens. Early token-detector members for " cub" drive it.
result.label: " cub" in cubic

result.description: Fires on adjectives like "significant", "notable", "fundamental" right after "there were/have been" introducing a plural noun of change or development. It stays silent on "significant" after verbs like "experienced", "seen", or "made".
result.label: Significant/notable after "there were"

result.description: Fires on connecting function words (and, to, with, the) after a micro-scale term in "bridge micro and macro" phrasing, where the next word is expected to be the macroscopic counterpart. Silent on ordinary "and" elsewhere.
result.label: Micro-to-macro connector words

result.description: Fires on the words "urban" and "rural" (also suburban, metropolitan) when they modify a following noun like areas, communities or planning. Members are mostly detectors of urban/rural tokens. Predicts nouns such as cores, context, frameworks.
result.label: urban / rural modifier words

result.description: Fires on the 'our' piece in 'fl-our-ish' (flourished/flourishing), after 'fl', in the sense of thriving. Silent on 'our' elsewhere, such as 'troubadour' or a word-initial 'ourishing'. Promotes 'ish' suffix continuations.
result.label: 'our' inside flourish

result.description: Fires on varied function words and punctuation (commas, "and", "or", "the", "\(") mid-sentence in expository technical text, often right before a noun phrase continues. No single token or clear construction dominates; the contrast commas in lists are silent.
result.label: Mid-sentence function words, expository text
Period in geometry/circle text
result.description: Fires on sentence-ending periods, mainly at the end of a paragraph, in geometry text about angles, circles and polygons. It stays silent on periods ending paragraphs in statistics or applied-research text. Logits favour angle- and circle-related tokens.

Fires on the piece "an"/"An" when it starts a word, such as the Buddhist term anatta/anicca/Anatman or "Ancient", in Buddhist/philosophy text. It stays silent on "an" inside words like emancipation or Nagarjunan.
result.label: Word-initial "an" piece (anatta)

result.description: Fires on the word piece " layer" (also "ayer") when it is the stem of a derived form like layering, layered or layeration, especially in baking and art technique text. It predicts suffixes and related words.
result.label: layer as stem of layering

result.description: Fires on ' such' when it follows a noun (category or list head) and introduces examples, as in "X such as Y". Silent when 'such' is a determiner ("such problems"). Members predict ' as' next.
result.label: 'such' introducing examples (such as)

result.description: Fires on abstract head nouns like quantity, property, factor, element, marker after an adjective ("an essential property", "a dimensionless quantity") when a technical concept is being characterized. Silent in some cases of the same token.
result.label: Abstract attribute nouns in definitions

result.description: Fires mainly on the adverb ending "-ively" in "played progressively (more/greater)", and on similar adjective/adverb pieces after "play(s)" ("crucial", "disproportionate", "incredibly") where a comparative or "role" is expected next.
result.label: "play progressively more" adverb ending
Closing quote after work title
result.description: Fires on the closing quotation mark (occasionally a closing apostrophe or parenthesis) right after the title of a book, play, opera or magazine, typically before a date or "and". Silent on plain prose without a quoted title.

Fires on varied tokens (commas, ' column', ' chemical') inside lists of sample or method characteristics in analytical chemistry/chromatography text, such as "sample characteristics such as chemical composition". Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Chromatography sample-property lists

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens: ' the', long dash lines, commas, and word pieces like 'ary'. No dominant token or clear condition; contrast shows ' the' often silent. Members are generic and weakly specific.
result.label: Mixed function tokens and dash lines

result.description: Fires on commas (and 'and') separating items in a list of math terms, especially trigonometric functions like sine, cosine, secant, or probability concepts. Silent on commas after clauses or introducing explanations.
result.label: Commas in math term lists

result.description: Fires on a mix of tokens: the digit '2' or '3' in fractions like 1/2 cup, and ' O'/'O' inside capitalized acronyms like ODEAs. The weaker contexts are mixed. The evidence is thin and inconsistent.
result.label: Fraction digits and capital O acronyms

result.description: Fires on adjectival or modifier words (fluid, cellular, muscular, material, modern, nuclear, human, computer) that precede a science or technology field noun, in academic science text. Predicts field words such as physics, biology, astronomy.
result.label: Modifier before science field noun

result.description: Fires on the space or token just before the next term in a mathematical sequence listing (e.g. "0, 1, [ ]2", "determine any term"), where a number comes next. Silent on a space before a standalone number like a bound or value.
result.label: Next term in number sequence

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ative'/'ive' when it completes "innovative" or "inventive", before a noun like approaches, solutions or technologies. It stays silent on 'ative' in creative, collaborative, narrative and imperative.
result.label: innovative/inventive suffix

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and mid-phrase tokens (' the', ' and', ' this', ' from', "'s") in abstract expository prose, where a noun phrase is expected next. No clear single trigger; the circuit failed and members are diffuse.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires on adjectives like "diverse"/"varied" in "meet the diverse needs of" in IT/organizational definitions, with weaker firing on other words in that kind of text. Silent on "diverse" in a different phrase ("tackle diverse industrial issues"). Evidence is mixed.
result.label: "meet the diverse needs" in IT text

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and connectors (using, of, the, its, over, growing) in formal expository text, where a noun or technical term is expected next. Peaks are inconsistent, and the same tokens such as ' using' are often silent in other contexts.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires on a comma after a noun phrase in a list of benefits or outcomes (e.g. "higher turnover rates, better satisfaction, improved results"), where the next item is a positive comparative like better, greater, improved. Silent on commas after clauses.
result.label: Comma in benefit/outcome lists

result.description: Fires on varied function words and punctuation (such "as", "including", "the", commas, "play" in role-play) that introduce a list of fields or applications, such as environmental monitoring. Predicts nouns like measurement or detection. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Lists of fields/applications introducers

result.description: Fires on "such as" and the start of fractions like "1/3" in lists of measuring cup and spoon sizes in cooking and measurement text. It stays silent on "1" in number theory contexts.
result.label: Measuring-cup fraction list items

result.description: Fires on linking prepositions or verbs like "of", "using", "through", "with" after nouns such as "use" or "work" in biomedical text (immunotherapy, personalized medicine). It predicts a medical or biological term next. It is silent on "using" in non-medical text.
result.label: Biomedical method-linking prepositions

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly " of", " at", "gent", " spin") inside dense physics prose on quantum, condensed-matter and magnetism topics, where a technical noun phrase continues. Peak tokens are mixed and the same " at" is silent in other contexts.
result.label: Function words in physics prose

result.description: Fires on prepositions like "for", "of", "to", "within" in energy and power-generation text (electricity for distribution, production of goods, types of engines), where the next word is likely an energy or engine term. Silent on "for" in generic contexts.
result.label: Prepositions in energy/power generation text

result.description: Fires on function words (of, varying, different, their) right before a noun like "abilities" or "disabilities", in accessibility/inclusive-design text about users with varying abilities. Predicts "capabilities". Silent on "of" in other topics.
result.label: Range of user abilities (accessibility)

result.description: Fires on mid-phrase word pieces like 'ent' in "Present Continuous" and 'g', plus some ' and'/' with' after a topic noun. It is silent on 'ent' in coherent/prevalent. The evidence is mixed and the peaks are scattered.
result.label: Scattered word-piece 'ent' in Present

result.description: Fires on ' of' right after "evolution", "history", "development" or "progression", where a field or practice is about to be named (evolution of music genres). It stays quiet on ' of' after "understanding", "exploration", "traits" or "language".
result.label: ' of' after evolution/history nouns

result.description: Fires on scattered function and process words (the, includes, conduct, investig-, detailed) in legal/regulatory process text, where the next word is likely a task like drafting, assessing or licensing. Peaks are inconsistent; the same ' the' stays silent elsewhere.
result.label: Legal process step-introducing words

result.description: Fires on digits ('4', '2', '3') inside long digit strings or ID-like codes, and weakly on ' the' or similar function words. Silent on '4' in years or ordinary numbers. Evidence is mixed and the logits are incoherent.
result.label: Digits inside code-like number strings

result.description: Fires on the word piece " libert" (libertarian, liberties) when it is a split-off stem that continues into a suffix such as -arian or -ies. Silent on the whole word "liberalism" and "freedoms".
result.label: ' libert' word-piece stem

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verb pieces (of, to, conduct/conducting, SA) in testing, evaluation and security-assurance text, where a testing or assessment verb is expected next. Silent on 'of' in generic phrases like 'success of'.
result.label: Testing/evaluation context connector tokens

result.description: Fires on connecting words (" into", " and", " with", " that") in text about dividing images into grids of lines (rule of thirds). Predicts a number or part word like "nine". Silent on "into" meaning transform into.
result.label: "into" in grid-division composition text

result.description: Fires on the piece 'b' (or 'box') inside the word "carbonyl"/"carboxylic" in organic chemistry text, where the word continues. Silent on 'b' in other words such as hyperbulb or hydrocarbons.
result.label: car-b-onyl / car-box-ylic word piece

result.description: Fires on function words (' the', ' of', ' and') mid-sentence in essay-style text about historical or artistic periods, often after a noun like "type" or "halls". It stays silent on many ' the' tokens in similar text, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Function words in history-art essays

result.description: Fires on the split-word piece ' ent' when it begins "entanglement" right after "quantum" (predicting 'ang'). It stays silent on ' ent' after other words such as "establishing", "include" or "understanding".
result.label: 'ent' of "quantum entanglement"

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces like 'ym' in "Polymer", 'ism', 'ch' in title-like lists of academic subjects or headings at document start; silent on 'ism' inside biology words like organism or metabolism. Mixed, weak evidence.
result.label: Word-piece in subject-heading lists

result.description: Fires on the word-initial prefix ' un' as a separate token, mostly after "an" or "the" before adjectives like unprecedented, unparalleled, unrelenting. Members are mostly ' un' detectors. Silent on unrelated text.
result.label: ' un' prefix before adjective

result.description: Fires on varied words (' logical', ' the', 's') in network topology text, where the next word is likely 'topology/layout'-type. Members are network/routing detectors. Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Network topology layout slot

result.description: Fires on varied words (framework, construct, commas, "of", "a") inside quantum computing and computer-science explanations, where the next word is likely a technical term such as quantum. Members are quantum-topic detectors. Peaks are scattered and weak.
result.label: Quantum computing text, scattered positions

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' tr' when it begins "trend"/"trends"/"trendy" after a determiner or adjective (this, emerging, a). It is silent when ' tr' starts the document or follows "fleeting". Predicts 'end' next.
result.label: ' tr' starting "trend"

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' prof' when it begins a longer word such as proficient, proficiency or profound. Members are mostly ' prof' detectors, and the next-token logits favour continuations like 'ic', 'essions' and 'ound'.
result.label: ' prof' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on words like "different", "across", "entire", "whole" in statistics/regression text about how variables' influence varies across points of a distribution (e.g. quantile regression). Silent on "different" in other statistical contexts.
result.label: "across different" in quantile regression text

result.description: Fires on the 'ce' piece inside "pharmaceutical" (also radiopharmaceuticals, biopharmaceutical), predicting the continuation 'ut'. Members are detectors of the pharma-/-ce- fragment and 'ut' continuation.
result.label: 'ce' in pharmaceutical

result.description: Fires on varied tokens in academic text, mostly hyphens in compound words (path-connected), also ' the', ' Political', ' finite'. Silent on some hyphens (non-meager, K-theory). Evidence is mixed; the logits are not informative.
result.label: Hyphens in technical compounds, mixed

result.description: Fires on function words (are, is, in, "voc") after a noun phrase in text about language, collocations and vocabulary, e.g. "pairings that are", "combination that is". Silent on "are" in other topics. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Function words in collocation/language text

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens: ' sh' in "shifts", digits and slashes in dates or number strings, and function words like "of", "and", "am". No clear shared meaning. The circuit fails, with weak faithfulness and diffuse members.
result.label: Mixed tokens: sh, slashes, digits

result.description: Fires on ' waves' and on ' that' right after a wave-type subject (e.g. "sound waves that"), where a verb like propagate or travel is expected next. Silent on ' that' after non-wave nouns such as data or molecules.
result.label: Wave subject awaiting verb

result.description: Fires on ' can', ' to' or ' that' right after a plural subject like "systems", "interfaces" or "models" in tech/AI text, where a capability verb (learn, predict, adjust) comes next. Silent on prepositional 'to' (related to, close to).
result.label: Modal 'can'/'to' after AI systems

result.description: Fires on ' and' (sometimes ' or') ending a list of verb phrases (e.g. "emphasize concepts, and improve…"), where a new verb is expected next. Silent on ' and' before noun items in lists.
result.label: 'and' before next verb in list

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece 'ci' inside words like reproducibility, conducive, and on 'us' in Modus; weaker on ' the' and a few others. Predicts word-continuation pieces (pher, b, bles, ve). Mixed, low-faithfulness circuit.

result.description: Fires on commas and conjunctions (", and", " as", " including") separating items in a list of components or factors, especially technical or enumerated nouns like drill parts. Stays silent on commas in lists of senses. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: List separators in enumerations

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments like ' Lav' (Lavoisier) and ' Lang', plus occasional ' maintain' or ' r' mid-word, predicting a word continuation (e.g. 'oisier'-like suffix pieces). Silent on plain name lists. Evidence is mixed.

result.description: Fires on the 've' piece in "conducive" (as in "an environment conducive to"), and weakly on other mid-word pieces like 'ctu' in sanctuary. Silent on 've' in "evolve". Members are diffuse and generic.
result.label: 've' in "conducive"

result.description: Fires on the word " mass" used as a modifier before a noun, as in mass production, mass media, mass manufacture, mass spectrometry. Predicts continuations like production, media, -ively. The contrast text lacks the token.
result.label: ' mass' as noun modifier

result.description: Fires after a long plural or compound subject noun phrase in abstract academic-style prose (e.g. "X and Y, ... [,] construct"), at the point where the main verb is expected. Peaks on commas, ' will', ' that'. Silent on commas that open participial clauses.
result.label: Subject-end before main verb

result.description: Fires on " fundamental" as an adjective right after "a" or "A" introducing a noun phrase (e.g. "a fundamental concept"). It stays quiet in predicate position after "is", after "two", or after "offer".
result.label: "a fundamental" before a noun

result.description: Fires on the word " our" as a possessive after a verb (shape, enhance, construct, influence) in abstract, academic-style text, before nouns like understanding or experiences. Silent after prepositions like "based on", "due to", "between", "of" in some cases.
result.label: Possessive 'our' after verbs

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' sed' (as in sediment, sedimentary), predicting the continuation 'iment'/'iments'. Members are mostly ' sed' detectors; weak activation on similar word-start fragments like 'ann', 'multip', 'cond'.
result.label: ' sed' start of sediment

result.description: Fires on adjectives or word pieces describing tempo, pace, or energy of music, dance and narrative (rapid, fluid, lively, intense, continuous). Members detect music context and speed words (faster, slower, calm). Silent on generic 'ed' verb endings elsewhere.
result.label: Tempo/pace descriptors in music and dance

result.description: Fires on the document-boundary/newline token (shown as ¶) that ends a short list item or sentence, where a new topic line or document may start. Silent on some similar boundaries, e.g. after "Management." or "unique.". Predicts a capitalized new-line start.
result.label: Boundary token after list items

result.description: Fires on function words (its, and, the, by, of, yet) inside descriptions of music, genres and instruments, where a descriptive adjective or noun about sound is expected next. Silent on the same words in non-music text. Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Function words in music descriptions

result.description: Fires on sentence-ending periods (and colons) after short title or heading-like phrases in chemistry/atomic-structure text, e.g. "Electron Configuration." Stays silent on periods after headings in other subjects.
result.label: Period after atomic-structure headings

result.description: Peaks are scattered across varied tokens (commas, 'the', 'to', suffix pieces) in technical text about software, engineering and devices. The next-token logits lean towards words like spatial, interaction, overlap and work. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed.

result.description: Fires on the word piece " Reyn" at the start of "Reynolds" (Reynolds number, Osborne Reynolds), in fluid-dynamics text. Members are mostly Reyn detectors plus other word-start piece detectors.

result.label: Scattered function words in abstract prose

result.description: Fires on " the" directly after a verb like highlighted, demonstrated, illustrates, revealed, or a phrase like "reminder of" or "testament to", where an abstract noun (consequences, challenges, importance) is expected next. Silent on " the" after plain "of".
result.label: "the" after highlighting/demonstrating verbs

result.description: Fires on the plural nouns or labels naming the bodies in the zeroth law of thermodynamics (' systems', ' objects', ' B' in "system A and B") when two or more systems are in thermal contact. Silent on 'systems' in generic property statements.
result.label: Thermal-equilibrium systems being paired

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " Sp"/" sp" (Spelling, spices, spending, spin), a split-off beginning of a longer word. Predicts continuations like "elling", "anning", "atial", "ices". Silent on other S-words such as Series.
result.label: Word-initial " Sp" fragment

result.description: Fires on 'opol' in "geopolitical" and on " that" after "culinary technique/cooking method" (relative clause introducing a description). Mixed peaks across two unrelated contexts; weaker hits on other science word pieces.
result.label: geopol- piece and 'technique that'

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' perce' in perceive/perceived/perception, mostly after "is/was/be/people", and predicts the suffix 'ived'/'iving'. Members are mostly ' perce' detectors plus similar prefixes like surv, rev, pract.
result.label: ' perce' prefix of perceive

result.description: Fires on the 'uz' piece in "fuzzy" (f|uz|zy), mainly in fuzzy logic/sets/relations text. Members are mostly 'uz' detectors from earlier layers; it predicts the following 'zy'.
result.label: 'uz' in "fuzzy"

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and punctuation (commas in lists, ' of', ' the', ' a', ' with') in expository academic or technical prose. The peaks share no single token and the contrast evidence is mixed, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires on varied function words (are, in, is, and, -ively) in text about computer memory hierarchy and caches, where the next word would be a memory/cache term. Silent on "are" in chemistry/physics text. Members are cache and memory topic detectors.
result.label: Function words in memory-hierarchy text

result.description: Fires on the 'D' in "3D" (also "dimensional" in "three-dimensional"), in contexts about 3D modeling, printing and graphics. Members are mostly 'D' detectors. The contrast text lacks the token.
result.label: 3D 'D' token

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (a, the, and, to, 's, include, by) in technical or engineering-style text, mainly where a noun like a process or quantity is expected next. Logits favor words like high, rapid, break. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Function words in technical prose

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces of long adjectives like "multif-ac-eted" (mostly 'ac', also 'et') and 'pre' in "unprecedented", where the word is still incomplete. Mostly one word, multifaceted, in essay-style text.
result.label: multifaceted / unprecedented word-piece

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (of, by, with, using, later) in texts about writing systems, scripts, numerals and languages. The members point to scripts, alphabets and numerals, but the peaks are mixed and the same ' of' often stays silent.
result.label: Function words in writing-system text
Initial G of acronym in parentheses
result.description: Fires on the capital 'G' that begins an acronym after an opening parenthesis, as in "Geographic Information Systems (GIS)". It predicts the acronym's remaining letters. It stays silent on 'G' inside a word like ArcGIS.

Fires on the word-start piece " sav" in "savings", mostly after "cost" (cost savings), predicting the "ings" continuation. Weakly fires on other split word starts like "ir" in irradiance and "territ".
result.label: " sav" in "cost savings"

result.description: Fires mainly on " trade"/" Trade" (especially in "trade-offs") and on a few other scattered tokens like " So" in "Soil" at heading starts. Predicts "-offs" continuations. Mixed, polysemantic peaks.
result.label: trade of trade-offs, mixed

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' myth' (mostly as the start of myth-ology, myth-ological, myth-ical, myths). Members are mainly ' myth' detectors across layers. It is silent on a text about tales that doesn't use the word.
result.label: ' myth' token detector

result.description: Fires on the start of a chemistry term, such as 'P' in a polymer abbreviation like (PET) or (PLA), ' py' in pyruvate, 'Co' in CoA, or 'h' in dihydroxy. It stays quiet on 'P' at the end of ATP or RuBP.
result.label: Chemical term-initial fragment (P, py, Co)

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments of long technical or academic words, mostly the 'polit' piece in socio-political/geopolitical, also 'cio', 'mon', 'orth', 'ag' in crystal-system names. It fires where the word is incomplete and a continuation piece is expected.
result.label: Word-start fragments in academic terms

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' liv' when it begins a longer word such as livestock or livelihoods, where a continuation like 'est' or 'elihood' comes next. Weak on similar pieces like ' alg'.
result.label: ' liv' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on ' especially' (or ' particularly') right after a copula like "is/are/becomes", as in "is especially true/important". Silent when it follows a comma introducing a noun-phrase qualifier ("..., especially for readers").
result.label: "is especially" after copula

result.description: Fires on verbs or prepositions right after an abstract subject that introduce what it covers or how (involves, comprises, includes, by, "also called"), in definitional passages about policy, finance or social topics. Peaks are mixed and weakly consistent.
result.label: Definitional verbs introducing scope or means

result.description: Fires mid-word on word pieces such as 'l' in "cutlery" and 'ens' in "utensil", plus occasional other mid-word pieces. It stays silent on 'l' in other words like "bowl" or "proliferation", so it needs the specific word.
result.label: Mid-word piece in cutlery/utensil

result.description: Fires on function words (' by', ' a', ' include', commas) in explanatory text about how something functions or contributes, e.g. "it acts as [a]" or "providing [added]". Silent on passive agent "by". Evidence is mixed; the logits are weak.
result.label: Function-role slot in explanatory text

result.description: Fires on 'ification' in the "[clarification needed]" editorial tag, and on ' needed' or placeholder slots like "Case Study 2 Description..." inside bracketed annotations. Silent on 'ification' in other words (stratification, gamification).
result.label: clarification-needed bracket tag

result.description: Fires on the word piece " Mag" at the start of a word that continues as "net-" (Magnetic, Magnets), including at the start of a heading. It pushes towards continuations like "net". It stays silent on the full word "magnetic".
result.label: ' Mag' before 'net' word piece

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' the', ' of', ' for', '/', ' to', ' through') in the middle of a phrase, mostly where a noun phrase follows. Peaks are inconsistent and the target is silent on many ' the' cases, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered function words before noun phrase

result.description: Fires on varied function words (for, while, in, commas) in technical text about measurement, statistics and data, where the next word is likely a measure or metric term. Peaks are scattered and the contrast is inconsistent, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: Function words before measure terms

result.description: Fires diffusely on function words and periods in academic or technical expository text (e.g. ' its', ' and', ' the', '.'), mid-sentence where a technical noun or verb is likely next. It is silent on periods that end a sentence before a paragraph break. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Diffuse function words in academic prose

result.description: Fires on a comma after an item in a list of abstract plural nouns (interests, behaviors, strategies, beliefs), where the list continues with more items and "and/or". Silent on clause-level or after-phrase commas.
result.label: Comma inside abstract-noun lists

result.description: Fires on a comma that ends a clause describing a cause-and-effect change in science text (e.g. "the barrier lowers,"), where a participle like "allowing", "enhancing" or "reducing" comes next. Silent on commas before "which" or in definitions.
result.label: Comma before consequence participle

result.description: Fires on function words or modifiers (the, of, on, specific, new, essential) that follow a verb or preposition in abstract mathematical or technical prose, where a mathematical noun is expected next. Silent on many identical ' the' contexts, so the cue is unclear.
result.label: Function words before math nouns

result.description: Fires on function words (' the', possessive 's, ' its') right before a noun in computing-history text, such as operating systems, GUIs and Unix. It stays quiet on ' the' before dates or periods like "the 20…" or "the 19…".
result.label: the/'s before computing noun

result.description: Fires on ' we' as the subject right after "the way" (or "how"), as in "transformed the way we interpret...". Silent on ' we' in other clauses such as "As we move" or "we can expect". Weaker on "the way people".
result.label: 'we' after "the way"

result.description: Fires on the verb "facilitate" (facilitates/facilitating/facilitate) and similar enabling words like "allows for", where a verb is about to be followed by an object such as communication or access. Silent on other -ating words like communicating.
result.label: facilitate / enable verbs

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verbs (contribute, the, and, 0) inside text about data normalization, scaling and standardization of features. Members are statistics and scaling topic detectors; the peak token itself is not consistent.
result.label: Data scaling/normalization text slots

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments that begin a longer word, mostly ' cap' (cap-and-trade, capillary, capability) and ' x' in 'xylem', where the next piece is a continuation. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low.
result.label: Word-initial fragment 'cap' / 'x'

result.description: Fires on connectives (" and", " of", " including", " or") inside lists or noun phrases in war and resource-loss history text, such as "resources, including manpower and materiel". Silent on "and" after comma-separated lists in other contexts.
result.label: Connectives in wartime resource lists

result.description: Fires on the word-initial fragment ' dev' (before 'astate', 'oting', 'otional'), where the next piece completes a split word. Weaker on other incomplete word starts like ' St' in 'Stellar', 'un-im-provised'.
result.label: ' dev' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' more', ' break', ' them', ' next', 'in', 'Complete') at points where a short completion follows, mostly in customer-service or advice text. The peaks are mixed and the contrast shows ' more' silent in comparatives, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: Scattered tokens in service-advice text

result.description: Fires on varied function words and modifiers (native, for, his, complex, robust, berg) mid-phrase in technical or academic prose, where a noun or abstract concept is expected next. Silent on 'berg' in Gutenberg. Evidence is mixed and low-consistency.
result.label: Mid-phrase modifiers before abstract nouns

result.description: Fires on a comma that ends a full clause about culture, religion or society and is followed by a trailing elaboration (e.g. "with…", "often…", "their…"). It stays quiet on commas after introductory phrases and in simple lists.
result.label: Comma after clause, before elaboration

result.description: Fires on 're, are, be, being, just after a subject (often "they/we") in verb-slot positions where a participle or adjective like aware/willing/-ing is expected next. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low.
result.label: Copula/auxiliary before predicate complement

result.description: Fires on the capital ' N' token when it starts a new line or document, as the first letter of a word like Nuclear or Nouns. It is quiet on 'Martin' in a list of names. Next-token logits favour continuations such as 'ern', 'ray' and 'ock'.
result.label: Line-initial ' N' token

result.description: Fires on subject-position pronouns or relative words (' it', ' which', ' that') that follow a noun phrase or colon and start a clause describing what a biological system or organ does. It predicts a present-tense verb such as 'is', 'houses' or 'works'.
result.label: Relative/pronoun before verb in biology

result.description: Fires on function words (the, of, and, comma, with-the) in advice-style text where a manner or quality noun is expected next, like "with the same ease/precision" or "a touch of humor". Predicts quality nouns such as wit, skill, ease.
result.label: Function words before manner/quality nouns

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (of, the, in, and, these) in academic science text about physics, decay and vibrations. Peaks are inconsistent and it stays silent on 'of' in linguistics passages. The evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words in physics-science prose

result.description: Fires on the word " active" when it modifies a following noun like listening, participation or engagement, in communication or teamwork text. It stays silent on some " active" tokens in similar contexts, so the exact condition is unclear.
result.label: ' active' before listening/participation

result.description: Fires on relative/pronoun words (" which", " it", " that") and commas that follow a described subject and begin a clause about it, where a verb like "is/has/provides" is expected. Silent on some ", which" cases, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Clause-linking which/it/that after subject

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'im' inside "ferrimagnetism/ferrimagnetic", predicting a continuation like 'agnet'. It stays silent on 'im' in other words such as "mimics". Weak activation on other word pieces.
result.label: 'im' in ferrimagnetic

result.description: Fires on varied function words and word pieces (' the', 'ian', ' this', ' as') in art-history and arts text, such as "against the", "Egyptian", "French". Logits favor suffix pieces like 'ite'. Silent on 'the' in corporate-governance text. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Art-context function words and suffixes

result.description: Fires on ' is' (also ' was', ' being') right after a distributive subject like "every/each X", as in "each slide is a frame". Silent on ' is' after other subjects such as "this" or abstract nouns.
result.label: 'is' after each/every subject

result.description: Fires on function words (can, or, and, to, as) in text about music and emotional or mental effects, where a mood or emotion word is likely to come next. Silent on ' can' in other topics.
result.label: Function words in music-emotion text

result.description: Fires on the verb "are"/"is" (or "rather") right after an abstract subject like "mathematical truths" in philosophy-of-mathematics text about formalism vs. Platonism, where a claim about the nature of truth follows. Silent on "are" in ordinary or logic contexts.
result.label: Copula after "mathematical truths" in formalism

result.description: Fires diffusely on function words and word pieces (' an', ' of', ' for', ' the', ' and', 'ometric') in abstract academic prose, mid-phrase. Consistency is low and the contrast does not show a clear condition. Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Function words in academic prose
' execut' word-start before -ives
result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece ' execut' (as in "executives") when a noun-forming suffix like "-ives" is expected. It also fires weakly on other word starts like ' parent' and on some function words. The evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
Fires on the word piece ' fant' (start of "fantasy", "fantastical") when the word is mid-sentence, predicting the continuation "asy"/"astic". Silent when "fantasy" opens the text at document start.
result.label: ' fant' piece before "asy"

result.description: Fires on varied function tokens (commas, 'and', 'with', 'has', 'to') mostly inside lists or elaborations of a noun phrase in expository text; the peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is diffuse, with no clear discriminating members.
result.label: Diffuse list/connector punctuation latent

result.description: Fires on a copula or auxiliary (was/were/is) or an adverb right after it (often, largely, heavily) in passive or descriptive statements by an abstract subject, where a participle like "conducted" or "influenced" is expected. Silent on some "was" tokens in historical narration.
result.label: Copula/adverb before passive participle

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' ecc' (as in "ecclesiastical"), predicting a following "les…" continuation. Members include detectors of other word-start fragments (Rem, app, mon, oph) that also lead to "les"-type completions.
result.label: ' ecc' start of ecclesiastical

result.description: Fires mostly on ' the' (also 'through', 'ly', 'and') in abstract academic prose, right before an abstract noun like "interplay", "emergence", "study". Silent on 'the' before dates or fixed phrases such as "on the other hand".
result.label: 'the' before abstract noun, academic prose

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments of a word split across tokens (' dow' in downturn, ' pu', ' cro' in crochet), plus a few LaTeX openers. Seems to mark an incomplete word start awaiting a continuation. Mixed evidence, weak faithfulness.
result.label: Word-start fragment tokens (dow, cro, pu)

result.description: Fires on the word " informed" in "make informed (decisions)", mostly business-analysis text. Members are detectors of " informed" that push toward "decision", "choices", "consent". Weaker on other adjectives after "make", like "appropriate" or "better".
result.label: "informed" in "make informed decisions"

result.description: Fires on ' setting' (also ' set'/'sets') as a verb after a comma or relative clause, in idioms like "setting the stage", "setting new records", "setting it apart". Members are detectors of set/setting and similar verbs like laid.
result.label: verb 'setting' in idioms

result.description: Fires on ' marks' (also represents, signifies, marking) when a historical period or event is said to mark the beginning or a transition of something. Context is historical-era descriptions; the verb comes after a period or event subject.
result.label: Period 'marks' the beginning

result.description: Fires mostly on ' on' (also ' the', ' of', commas), strongest after "walking on" in the idiom-like "walking on a tight(rope)". Silent on other uses of ' on' (on the other hand, influence on). Peaks are scattered, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: 'on' after walking (tightrope)

result.description: Fires on the word piece " challeng" (and the following " pos" in "challenges posed"), mainly right after "the" in "Despite the challenges..." or "address the challenges posed by". It stays silent on "challenges" after "these" or "several", or after "poses".
result.label: "the challenges posed" phrase

result.description: Fires mostly on commas separating items in a list of abstract nouns or parallel verbs (e.g. "passion, authenticity", "designing, developing"), plus some " of" tokens. Silent on commas after clauses or introductory phrases. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weakly faithful.
result.label: Commas inside lists of abstract nouns

result.description: Fires on the article ' a' right after a cooking technique name (e.g. "Steaming, a" or "Steaming is a"), where a descriptive noun phrase defining the technique comes next. Silent on ' a' in other kitchen or food sentences.
result.label: 'a' after cooking technique name

result.description: Fires on ' well' as the first piece of "wellbeing"/"wellness" (e.g. "mental well-being", "physical wellness"), predicting "being", "-" or "ness". Silent on "as well as" and on some "wellness programs" cases.
result.label: ' well' in wellbeing/wellness

result.description: Fires on function words and punctuation (' a', ',', 'with', '(') in culinary text where a list of flavors, textures or tools is being offered or described; predicts culinary terms like 'sous', 'mise'. Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Culinary description function words

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' ph' (also ' Ph') when it begins a word like phonetic or phonemic, mostly in linguistics text. It is silent when ' ph' starts the document. It predicts 'on' as the next piece.
result.label: ' ph' before phonetic/phonemic

result.description: Fires on ' and' that follows the object of "goes beyond / transcends / rejected traditional X", where the sentence continues with a further verb or contrast (instead, into). Silent on ordinary coordinating 'and' in lists or pairs.
result.label: 'and' after "goes beyond X"

result.description: Fires on scattered word pieces that begin a word or phrase and need a continuation, such as ' rad' (radar), ' exhib' (exhibitions), ' up', and sometimes ' the'. The peak tokens are mixed and the evidence is weak; the logits favour word-start continuations like 'rag' and ' situ'.
result.label: Mixed incomplete word-start pieces

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and fragments (the, with, used, _, of) in passages about origins or early history of science and ideas. It predicts source-like nouns (base, root, source). Peaks are inconsistent, and the same token is often silent elsewhere.
result.label: Function words in origins-of-science text

result.description: Fires on "between" and nearby function words (the, to, and) in phrases like "relationship/connection between the nervous system and...", mostly in biology or science text. Silent on "between" after some nouns like interplay or interactions, so the pattern is mixed.
result.label: Relationship-between in science text

result.description: Fires on the prefix " non" and the hyphen right after "non" (non-linear, non-homogeneous, non-normal), predicting the word piece that follows. It stays silent on hyphens in other compounds like second-order or large-scale.
result.label: "non" prefix and its hyphen

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and punctuation (commas, 'of', 'to', 'the', 'stone', 'back') in academic or expository text, mid-phrase where a noun or compound continuation is expected. No single token dominates; the same comma often stays silent.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase function tokens

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens (commas in lists, ' loss' in "lossless", ' is' in "isomerism") where a word or list item is followed by a continuation. Silent on many commas in similar lists. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is unfaithful.
result.label: Mixed commas and word-piece splits

result.description: Fires on the word piece " expl" when it begins a word like exploration, explorer or explored. Members are mostly " expl" detectors. It stays silent on some " expl" tokens, such as at text start, and the contrast doesn't clearly show why.
result.label: ' expl' start of exploration

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens: 'tr' word pieces (Altruism, filtrate) plus function or modifier words like 'and', 'shared', 'including', 'necessary' that precede a noun in a list or phrase. Evidence is mixed and low-consistency.
result.label: Mixed 'tr' piece and connector words

result.description: Fires mostly on ' government' (also party, company, annual, school) when it is a modifier noun right before a record-type noun like reports, publications, statistics. Predicts such nouns next. Silent on 'government' used as a standalone subject.
result.label: Government as modifier before reports

result.description: Fires on 'ights' in "insights" and on " insight", mainly in "gain/provide valuable insight(s) into ..." phrasing. It predicts " into". It is silent when "insights" is a subject or sits sentence-finally.
result.label: insight(s) before 'into'

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' bro' when it is likely to continue as "broader", mostly after "provides/offering/providing" in academic text. It pushes the next token towards 'ader'. Weakly active on other word-start pieces.
result.label: ' bro' predicting 'broader'

result.description: Fires on 'ing' ending of adapt/adjust (also ' adapt', ' adjust' themselves) in communication-skill text, where an object like "one's approach" or "to" follows. Silent on 'ing' in other verbs such as developing, maintaining, respecting.
result.label: adapt/adjust verb, especially -ing

result.description: Fires on ' not' right after a copula like "is" or "are" (e.g. "Wine is not just..."). It predicts hedging continuations such as only, just, merely, solely, necessarily. It stays silent on "do not" and "let's not".
result.label: "is not" before just/only/solely

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' to', ' of', ' the', 'net', 'gold', 'dollars') in expository passages, with no single dominant token. Members are mostly generic function-word hubs, so the evidence is mixed and the circuit failed.
result.label: Scattered function-word peaks in expository text

result.description: Fires on ' of' right after "the state" in descriptions of entangled particles, where the next word is "another/the other/its partner". It stays silent on other 'of' uses like "heart of" or "flow of".
result.label: "state of" before another particle

result.description: Fires on function words (how, to, of, that, more) mid-sentence in explanatory text defining properties like permeability, resistance or toughness. It seems to anticipate a property-related continuation. Silent on 'how' in philosophy contexts. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words in physical-property definitions

result.description: Fires on " the" right after "at" when it begins a scale phrase like "at the individual/national/macro level". Silent on "the" after other prepositions. Members detect "at" plus level-words and push toward "level".
result.label: "the" after "at" (level phrases)

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and punctuation (' of', '.', ' the', 'ing') in abstract academic or essay prose about art, science and math. Silent on many other ' of' tokens, and the evidence does not show what separates them.
result.label: Scattered function words in academic prose

result.description: Fires on the noun ending a historical-period phrase, mainly ' era' and ' period' after a period name (the Classical era, late medieval period). Silent on some 'era' tokens, e.g. after 'This' or 'pre-recorded', so the cause is unclear.
result.label: Historical era/period noun

result.description: Fires on ' both' right after a preposition (in/for/to both), where a paired "both X and Y" is expected. It is silent on ' both' after a verb or "are", as in "are both effective".
result.label: 'both' after a preposition

result.description: Fires on ' in' right after "ways" when a relative clause follows ("the ways in which..."). It predicts "which" or "whom" next. It stays silent on ordinary ' in' after nouns such as "aids in" or "found in".
result.label: "ways in which" preposition

result.description: Fires on the word " nuclear" (and "lear" in "Nuclear") when it is followed by something like reactor, power, facilities or weapons. It pushes the next token toward reactor and facility words.
result.label: ' nuclear' predicting reactor/facility

result.description: Fires on ' the' in abstract expository text, where it starts an abstract noun phrase after a preposition, comma or conjunction (e.g. "through the meticulous…"). Predicts nouns like use, inclusion, incorporation. Silent on 'the' before story or author subjects.
result.label: 'the' before abstract process nouns

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' cos' (also ' atmos') when it begins a word like cosmic, cosmos or cosine, and pushes the next token towards 'mic', 'mos' and similar continuations. Mostly seen in cosmology text.
result.label: ' cos' word-start before -mic/-mos

result.description: Fires on function words (a, the, any, in, for, various) in abstract expository text about discourse, argument, communication and philosophy, where the next word is likely "debate/discussion/exchange". Silent on the same words in other contexts. Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Function words before debate/discussion nouns

result.description: Fires mostly on ' d' in "moral/ethical dilemmas" (predicting "ilemma"), with weaker firing on some 'and'/'the' tokens. Silent on "the dilemma" singular after "the". Mixed, low-consistency circuit.
result.label: ' d' of moral dilemmas

result.description: Fires on relative pronouns ("that", "which") and modals ("can", "may") following a noun naming a problem, risk or cause, where a causal or effect verb is expected next (indicate, trigger, cause). Silent on some "that" uses, such as complementizers.
result.label: Relative 'that'/modal before effect verb

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and determiners (' all', ' these', ',', ' stored', ' respective') in abstract expository text on economics, finance and physics, mid-clause before a noun. Pushes toward economic nouns weakly. Evidence is mixed and the peak tokens are inconsistent.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (mostly ' and', also ' on', ' in', word pieces) in academic or abstract text, often after a topic term in a title-like pair such as "Uses and Gratifications". Silent on many other ' and' uses. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Academic term-pair 'and' connector

result.description: Fires on linking prepositions (to, by, with, saw) after a verb or participle that attributes a development to a cause, such as "thanks to", "driven by", "transformed by", "saw ... with", in tech-history prose. It predicts "the advent/development of" style nouns.
result.label: Causal prepositions before "advent of"

result.description: Fires on the token ' public' as a noun or adjective in the sense of the public sector, public at large or public goods, typically after "the". It stays silent in "public order" and "public-private", and predicts words like good, interest, eye and sector.
result.label: ' public' as in public sector

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and punctuation ('.', ' of', ' and', ' for', ' or') in expository text about water quality, monitoring and science, often where a subject seems dropped. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Function words in technical expository text

result.description: Fires on varied function words and word pieces (of, type, such, retain, closing paren) in geology text about volcanoes, where the next word is likely a volcano term like ash, lava or volcano. Silent on ' of' in other earth-science contexts.
result.label: Volcano-text slot before volcanic terms

result.description: Fires on emotion nouns (love, hope, happiness, joy) listed as items in a series of emotions, e.g. "basic emotions such as happiness, sadness". Silent when "love" is a verb ("I just love to"). Predicts further emotion words.
result.label: Emotion nouns in lists

result.description: Fires on function words (the, an, a, from, hyphen) in technical or explanatory text, mostly where a noun phrase is about to start. Silent on many ' the' tokens, and the evidence doesn't show what separates them.
result.label: Function words before technical noun phrase

result.description: Fires on the 'dis' piece in "inter|dis|ciplinary" (also 'if' in "mult|if|aceted"), predicting 'cipl'. It stays silent when 'dis' follows a hyphen with no 'inter' before it.
result.label: 'dis' in interdisciplinary

result.description: Fires on the 'r' token in "wide-r|anging", where a split-up word is being completed, and pushes the next token towards "anging". It is silent on 'r' in other words such as "neutrino". Members detect 'r', ' arr' and ' R' word-starts.
result.label: 'r' in wide-ranging

result.description: Fires on verbs and function words (create, communicate, validate, "creation of") in text about prototyping and product development, where the next word is likely "prototype", "mock", or "feedback". It stays silent on "creating" in general engineering text.
result.label: Prototyping verbs predicting prototype/mock

result.description: Fires on "to" in "due to" (also "because of", "faced", "encountered") where a cause or problem is introduced, predicting negative nouns like "poor", "limitations", "lack". Silent on some "due to" cases, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Causal "due to" before problems

result.description: Fires on 'ound' in "prof-ound" when it follows "have/had a" and predicts an impact/effect noun ("had a profound impact"). Silent when "profound" is followed by "-ly" or used attributively elsewhere (e.g., "profound symmetry").
result.label: profound before impact noun

result.description: Fires diffusely on function words and modifiers (' relatively', ' the', ' of', ' and') in expository text, mid-phrase where an adjective or noun is expected next. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Diffuse function-word slot before modifier

result.description: Fires on nouns for surrounding setting or circumstances (landscape, environment, conditions, threats, genre) in business/analysis text, often ending a noun phrase before a clause like "within which". Silent on "landscape" in a literary sense.
result.label: Surrounding environment/conditions nouns in analysis

result.description: Fires on the verb ' mirror' (mirror/mirrors/mirrored) meaning "reflect or resemble", with an abstract subject such as music, poetry or trends. Weaker on similar verbs like matches or rivals. Predicts an object like "those", "life" or "society".
result.label: verb 'mirror' meaning reflect

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' sh' when it begins a verb like shaping, shaped or shifting, mostly after "role in" or "been" in abstract academic text. It predicts continuations such as 'aping' and 'ifting'.
result.label: ' sh' start of shaping/shifting

result.description: Fires on word-start pieces ' facil', ' necess', ' precip' (also ' neces', ' prior', ' digit') where the next piece is likely "itate/itated". It predicts the "-itate" suffix continuation.
result.label: Stems before "-itate" suffix

result.description: Fires on the period ending a person's name (e.g. "Sergey Brin.", "Tim Cook.") in a list of names, one per line. Silent on periods after topic or subject headings in similar line-by-line lists.
result.label: Period after person name in list

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (the, to, involves, not) inside academic explanations of media influence and public opinion, where the next word is likely a media-effect noun or verb. Silent on 'the' in physics/materials text. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness.

result.description: Fires mostly on ' to' in "According to" at the start of a sentence or document, where a source or person is expected next. It also fires weakly on other prepositions, such as "complicated by". It stays silent on ' to' in other uses.

Fires on varied function words and nouns (" of", " type", " function", " loops") in technical math/science text, often right after a noun like "numbers of the second/first kind". Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weakly faithful.
result.label: Math terms: "numbers of the first kind"

result.description: Fires on function words (into, involves, is, on) right after "dataset" or "cross-validation" in explanations of k-fold splitting, where the next word is likely partition/subsets/k. Silent on "into" in other contexts like "data into manageable parts".
result.label: k-fold dataset splitting connectors

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and connectives (and, or, as, than, commas) and some words like "improved" in technical expository text. Peaks are inconsistent and the target is silent on many 'and' tokens in lists. The pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered connectives in technical prose

result.description: Fires on " due" in causal "due to" after a predicate (is largely due, effective due, doubt due). Members are mostly " due" detectors plus words like related/attributed. Silent on the contrast text, which lacks " due".
result.label: causal ' due' (due to)

result.description: Fires on the final piece 'voir' in "reservoir" in petroleum/reservoir engineering text, with weaker firing on subsurface/groundwater word-ends ('face', 'water'). Predicts physical-property nouns such as depth, pressure, flow.
result.label: reservoir 'voir' in petroleum text

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' to', 'RT', 'ci', ' sound') inside definitions of reverberation/decay time ("time for sound to decay by 60 decibels"). Silent on ' to' in unrelated history/humanities text. Circuit is weak and mixed.
result.label: Reverberation decay-time definition tokens

result.description: Fires on the word piece " fol" when it begins "folding"/"fold", mostly after "protein" or in other folding contexts. It pushes the next token toward "ding", "ds" or "ded". Silent on unrelated dough-layering text.
result.label: " fol" start of folding

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' subt' (start of subtle, subtlety, subtly), with weaker activation on ' bal'/'Bal' pieces. Upstream members are mostly ' subt' detectors. It is silent when ' subt' starts the document, so it needs preceding context.
result.label: ' subt' word-piece (subtle/subtlety)

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " intr" (intrinsic, intricate, intriguing), mostly in academic or descriptive text. Predicts continuations such as "insic", "usion", "ude". Upstream members are mostly " intr" detectors.
result.label: " intr" word-start piece

result.description: Fires on word pieces completing sense words like "sc-ent", "sm-ell", "arom-a", especially in smell/taste/flavor text; predicts suffixes such as "-ally" or "profiles". Silent on "ent" in unrelated words like "accentuating".
result.label: Scent/smell word-piece endings

result.description: Fires on chemistry/food-science noun pieces such as ' carbon', ' ice', ' acid', 'gen', and word-ending 'ter' (butter), and promotes continuations like ' cub', 'cre', ' dio'. Mixed tokens; the strongest members are carbon detectors.
result.label: Carbon/ice chemistry and food nouns

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' published', ' between', ' are', quote marks) in academic text about logic, mathematics and philosophy, such as Frege and Sinn. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: Logic/math academic prose, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires on function words (of, how, with, on, by) in geography-themed academic text, especially in definitions of the field of geography. It pushes toward spatial, regional and mapping words. The same words are silent in other humanities texts.
result.label: Function words in geography text

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments like ' Pro' (Prophase), ' De', ' N', ' F' that begin a longer word, apparently predicting a continuation such as 'ponents'. Silent on ' N' in other names (Art Nouveau). Members are generic, so the evidence is mixed.
