result.description: Fires on ' the' right after "during" (also "in the", "of the") when a time period or era is expected next, like "during the dot-com…" or "during the early…". Predicts period words such as early, late, mid, new.
result.label: 'the' before a time period

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece 'dis' in "interdisciplinary" or "transdisciplinary", predicting 'cipl'. It also fires on 'le' in the title "Role of...". Members are mostly 'dis' detectors. Peaks are mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: 'dis' in interdisciplinary (plus 'Role')

result.description: Fires on the verb " involves" (also " involve") after an abstract process noun subject like "analysis", "assessment" or "approach" in business or analytic text. It predicts a following action verb such as collect, comparing or measuring.
result.label: " involves" after process-noun subject

result.description: Fires on odd, fragmentary tokens: broken byte pieces, 'ampa', ' Germania', 'overline', ' où', Cyrillic fragments, 'std'. No shared meaning; the pattern looks like rare or mid-word pieces, and the logits are mixed.
result.label: Rare fragment tokens, mixed

result.description: Fires on example-introducing words (like, as, include, including) that follow "services" in ecosystem-services text, right before a list of examples such as provisioning or regulating services (food, water, climate regulation). Silent on "as" in other uses.
result.label: Ecosystem services example-list introducers

result.description: Fires on ' to' in a date range "from YEAR to ..." right after a year, where an end year or "the present/recent" is expected. Silent on ' to' as a preposition or infinitive marker.
result.label: "to" in year ranges

result.description: Fires on word endings of negative-leaning evaluative adjectives (confrontational, offensive, deceptive, antagonistic, disingenuous) describing how behaviors are perceived in cross-cultural communication. Silent on positive 'constructive/productive/attentive' -ive endings.
result.label: Negative perception adjective suffixes

result.description: Fires on the verb stem " discuss" right after a document-part subject like "section" or "part" (e.g. "section discusses"), where the next token is a verb suffix such as "es". Silent when a different verb follows "section".
result.label: "section discuss(es)" verb stem

result.description: Fires at the end of a decade or period noun phrase (e.g. "1930s", a period name followed by a comma or parenthesis), where a verb like "witnessed", "saw" or "marked" is predicted next. It is silent on "1970s" inside mid-sentence prepositional phrases.
result.label: Period subject awaiting "witnessed/saw"
' role' after "play a ... "
result.description: Fires on " role" (or " roles") in the idiom "play(s) a significant/crucial/important role", after the verb "play" and an adjective. It stays silent on "The role of..." where there is no "play".

Fires on scattered function words and commas (',', ' the', ' as', ' are', ' to', ' how') mid-sentence in expository text, often after statistics or process verbs. Logits favour adjectives like 'past', 'current', 'available', 'enough'. Evidence is diffuse and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Diffuse mid-sentence function words

result.description: Fires on connector tokens (such as, including, colon, of, and) right after a mention of "benefits", where a list of benefits comes next. Predicts words like reduced, increased, improved.
result.label: Connector introducing list of benefits

result.description: Fires on ' intellectual' as an adjective in historical or cultural-era text (Renaissance, periods of intellectual and cultural activity), predicting curiosity, awakening, energy. Silent when it opens a text with no preceding context.
result.label: ' intellectual' in cultural-history context

result.description: Fires on varied function words (of, and, their, by, for) after abstract nouns or verbs in expository text, where a noun phrase continues. Silent on 'of' after "understanding/use/processing". Evidence is mixed and the circuit is diffuse.
result.label: Function words after abstract nouns

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and verbs (the, of, to, that, retain, keep) mid-clause in expository text, where a noun or content word is expected next. Silent on "the" after "to" or "similar to". Evidence is mixed and the circuit unfaithful.
result.label: Mid-clause function words before noun

result.description: Fires on connecting words (mostly ' of', also commas and '-ing' pieces) in abstract, environmental or technical expository text, where the next word is a resource, substance or process noun. It stays silent on ' of' after some nouns like influx, surge or distribution.
result.label: ' of' before substance or process nouns

result.description: Fires on ' for' (sometimes ' of'/' to') right after a benefit noun like "happiness" or "benefit", where a beneficiary comes next (everyone, society, all, both). Silent on ' for' after verbs or phrases like "allows for" and "aim for".
result.label: ' for' after benefit noun, beneficiary next

result.description: Fires mostly on " stem" in "pluripotent stem cell" and similar biology text, plus scattered tokens in cell/biology passages where a cell-related noun is likely next. Silent on "neural stem" in the contrast. Predicts cell-type continuations.
result.label: Stem cell biology token before "cell"

result.description: Fires on ' has'/' have' right after an abstract subject noun like "Music" or "symbolism" in essay-style text about culture and art, predicting perfect-tense continuations ("has always", "has long", "been"). Silent on 'has' after "individuals".
result.label: has/have after abstract cultural subject

result.description: Fires on function words (the, of, and, to, from) in academic explanatory text about biology and language study, where the next word is likely a field-specific noun. Silent on the same words in other contexts. Evidence is mixed and the circuit's faithfulness is poor.
result.label: Function words in science/linguistics exposition

result.description: Fires on varied tokens ('ible' in irreversible, 'isions' in collisions, 'that', 'their', 'processes') in physics text about entropy and irreversibility, where a plural noun like processes or steps is expected next. Silent on 'ible' in 'audible'.
result.label: Entropy/irreversibility physics text, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and verb pieces (' the', ' has', ' requires', 'ing', ' all') in technical expository text, mostly where a verb or object is about to follow. Peaks are inconsistent. Logits weakly favor 'ret'/'reading'/'returning'.
result.label: Scattered function words in technical prose

result.description: Fires on ' the' after origin phrases such as "derived from", "originating from", "dating back to", "roots in", where a nationality, era or source is expected next. Stays silent on ' the' after other prepositions or verbs.
result.label: 'the' after origin-from phrases

result.description: Fires on connectives (and, or, comma, as, whereas) right after "Type I" or "Type II error" in hypothesis-testing text, where the next word is likely "Type" or "false". Silent on "and" in other statistics lists.
result.label: Connectives after Type I/II error

result.description: Fires on the token ' research' as a noun, usually after an adjective or possessive (earlier, pioneering, original research). Pushes the next token toward 'ers', institutions, facilities and 'conducted'. Members are mostly ' research' detectors in earlier layers.
result.label: ' research' token detector

result.description: Fires on ' it' (also 'model', 'concept') as the subject pronoun of a main clause that follows a concessive or contrastive clause ("Although it...", "While X was developed, it..."), predicting a verb like "still", "fallen", "wouldn't".
result.label: Subject 'it' after concessive clause

result.description: Fires on ' that' (occasionally ' which') as a relative pronoun after a plural event noun in historical or military text, like wars, battles or tensions. It is silent on 'that' after other nouns such as tapestry, kingdoms or anxiety.
result.label: Relative 'that' after historical events

result.description: Fires on plural noun endings (funds, expenditures, challenges, impacts, benefits, earnings) in finance/economics-style abstract text, mostly on nouns for gains, costs or losses. Predicts words like 'versus', 'against', 'losses', 'faced'. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low.
result.label: Plural cost/benefit nouns in economics text

result.description: Fires on forms of the verb "draw" (draws, drawing, draw), especially in the figurative sense "draws on/upon", "drawing from", "draw attention/connections". Predicts continuations like upon, from, parallel, connections.
result.label: verb "draw" (draws on/from)

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' Cal' when it begins a longer word, mostly in 'Calvin'/'Calvinist', predicting 'vin'. Weaker on other word-initial fragments such as ' Monte' and ' da'.
result.label: ' Cal' as start of Calvin

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' em' when it starts a longer word, most strongly in "fosters em|pathy" and also em|otion, em|issions, em|blem. It pushes the next token toward path, otion, anci.
result.label: ' em' word-start piece (empathy)

result.description: Fires on adjective-ending suffixes like -ized/-ined/-ated inside a noun phrase after "a/an", where a noun such as system, approach, or form is expected next. Silent on -ized verbs (emphasized, prioritized).
result.label: Adjective suffix before system/approach noun

result.description: Fires on the word piece " intr" at the start of words like intricate, intriguing, intrinsic, mostly after "the", "an" or "and". It pushes toward continuations such as "igue", "igu" and "icate". Upstream members are mostly " intr" detectors.
result.label: ' intr' word-start piece (intricate/intriguing)

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' inter' (prefix of interference, interrogative, interjection, interconnection) and pushes toward continuations like 'ference', 'vent', 'medi', 'dependencies'. Members are mostly ' inter' detectors across layers.
result.label: ' inter' prefix token

result.description: Fires on modal or auxiliary verbs (will, can, turn) right after a relative-clause subject like "relationships that" or "connections", where a verb such as help, allow, or enable is expected next. Common in self-help or communication advice text.
result.label: Modal verb after relative-clause subject

result.description: Fires on particles like ' away', ' off', ' back' right after a transitive verb such as peel, cut, or slice, where an object noun (layers, skin, excess) is expected next. Silent in contexts without a verb-particle construction.
result.label: Verb particle away/off after peel-cut verbs

result.description: Fires on the token " result" in the phrase "as a result (of)", also "is a result of". Members are mostly " result" detectors in earlier layers. Output pushes toward "of" and "-ant" continuations.
result.label: " result" in "a result of"

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece ' d' (a space-prefixed "d" that starts a longer word such as dough, dining, dishes, damping). Predicts continuations like "ough", "ining", "ishes". Silent on some ' d' before "ish" in other contexts.

result.description: Fires on ' own' following a possessive (their, its, your, narrators') as in "their own words" or "its own right". Predicts words like unique, right, distinct, kind.
result.label: Possessive + 'own'

result.description: Fires on the capital word-start token ' L' when a following word piece is expected (e.g. "Dough L|ayering", "L1", "Lucas number L"). Predicts continuations like 'ayer', 'anguages', 'ingu'. Peaks all in one document type.

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments like 'ht' in hashtag/fraught and 'qu' in earthquake, where the next piece is a suffix such as -ags or -ake(s). Logits boost 'ags', 'ake', 'akes', 'aking'.
result.label: Word-piece before -ags/-ake suffix

result.description: Fires on the article "a/an" or an evaluative adjective or word piece (essential, vital, crucial, integral) after "is/as a(n)", where a noun like factor, element, or attribute comes next. Quiet on "a" after "like" or "such as".
result.label: Adjective before role noun (is an essential...)

result.description: Fires on scattered modifier or comparative tokens (flexible, -er, -ier, existing, the) inside expository text about technology or language. It's diffuse and inconsistent, and silent on 'flexible' in a payment-methods context.

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments like ' Lar' (in "Law of Large Numbers") and ' sur', where the next piece completes the word (ge, plus, pass). Mostly peaks on ' Lar' in that phrase; weaker on ' sur', ' lon'.

result.description: Fires on varied function words and nouns (' to', ' which', commas, 'maintenance') inside text about software/system maintenance, where the next word is likely maintenance-related (repair, defects, maintenance). Silent on ' to' in unrelated contexts.
result.label: Maintenance-topic function words

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens, most often ' jour' (before "ney"), plus ' be', ' to', ' must' in scientific-proposition phrasing. Logits favor word-piece continuations like 'ne'/'ney'. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.

result.description: Fires on plural subject nouns (mostly ' characters', also experiences, phenomena, dialects) in abstract essay-like text, where a verb is expected next. It is silent on many other ' characters' occurrences, and the contrast doesn't show why.
result.label: Plural subject noun before verb

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' the', ' and', ' a', ' given') and 'essential' in expository technical text, often after verbs like identify, establish, or are essential. Contrast shows ' the' silent in other contexts. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is unfaithful.
result.label: Function words in expository definitions

result.description: Fires on ' the' directly after the preposition "on" (also "onto"), as in "on the surface", "on the other hand", "on the circle". Silent on ' the' after other words or prepositions. Predicts nouns like fly, part, outside.
result.label: ' the' right after "on"

result.description: Fires on the word "proof" (also "Proof", "proofs") as a noun in mathematical or logical text, e.g. "proof by contradiction" or "proof assistants". Weaker on non-math uses such as "proof public sites". Silent on general logical-argument text that lacks the word.
result.label: the word "proof"

result.description: Fires on the word "method"/"methods" (including before "-ology"), in technical or academic text about procedures or techniques. Pushes the next token toward "ologies"/"ology". Members include method-token detectors from earlier layers.
result.label: "method(s)" token, predicts -ology

result.description: Fires on function words (to, of, which, describe, denotes) right after the subject "perfect aspect" in English grammar explanations, where a description of what it expresses comes next. Quiet on the same words elsewhere in such texts.
result.label: Function words in perfect-aspect grammar text

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' called', ' and', ' with', 'ian', ' political') in academic or explanatory text, where the next word is a noun-like concept (' or', ' economic'). Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit failed.
result.label: Scattered function words in academic text

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' met' when it is the start of "metaphor(s)" in writing and literary-technique text, predicting the continuation 'aph'/'ap'. It stays quiet on ' met' as a whole word, such as "was met with", and on the already-complete "metaphoric".
result.label: ' met' beginning "metaphor"

result.description: Fires on the first piece of a split proper name, mainly ' Th' in "Law of Thermodynamics" and ' Lock' in "John Locke", and predicts the continuation piece (erm, e, hart). Silent on ordinary text.
result.label: Split name start: Th(ermodynamics), Lock(e)

result.description: Fires mainly on the "aving" piece in compound modifiers like "life-saving" or "energy-saving", just before a noun such as technology, equipment or practices. Weak activity on a few other tokens. The contrast text does not show what it needs.
result.label: -saving compound modifier suffix

result.description: Fires on linking words (" of", " with", " like", " as", commas) in history-of-linguistics/scholarship text where a scholar's name is expected next, e.g. "the work of", "century with". Silent on " of" in other topics.
result.label: Linking word before scholar name

result.description: Fires on the piece "ake" in "stakeholder" (st|ake), predicting "holder"/"hold"/"owner" next. Upstream members are mostly "ake" detectors in the same word.
result.label: "ake" in stakeholder

result.description: Fires on "literature" (also poetry, "Liter-ature") when it appears as an item in a list of arts and humanities fields (art, music, drama, film). Predicts nouns like reviews, festival, schools.
result.label: literature in arts lists

result.description: Fires on scattered function and modifier words (' and', 'both', ' including', ' increasing', ' food') in expository text, mostly where a conjunction or modifier precedes a further item. Logits favor prefixes like multi-, inter-. Evidence is mixed and diffuse.
result.label: Scattered connectives before prefixes

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens: 'ous' in "Continuous" (grammar tense headings), and scope/preposition words like 'across', 'throughout', 'including', 'of'. Evidence is mixed, with low consistency and a weak circuit fit.

result.description: Fires on function words and verbs (use, of, enables, through, where) in economics text, in slots where an economics-related word is likely to come next. Predicts economic/econom tokens. Silent on "of" in other fields like logic or philosophy.
result.label: Function words in economics text

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' elev' (as in elevate), and more weakly ' cultiv' (cultivate), where the next piece is likely a verb suffix like -ate/-ating. Logits favor completions such as 'fill', 'atable'.
result.label: ' elev' / ' cultiv' verb stem

result.description: Fires on varied function words (of, for, their, a, by, becomes) in essay-style text about writing, literature and storytelling techniques, where a noun like text, narrative or story is expected next. Silent on some 'their' cases in linguistics text.
result.label: Function words in literary-craft prose

result.description: Fires on ' a' right after "become/remains/is" (or a noun subject) when it introduces a predicate noun like "a crucial component" or "a challenge" in abstract expository text. Stays quiet on ' a' after other verbs such as "achieving", "led to" or "necessitate".
result.label: ' a' before evaluative predicate noun

result.description: Fires on the token 'K' inside the acronym QKD (Quantum Key Distribution), after 'Q', and predicts 'D' next. Other 'K' uses, like Runge-Kutta, are handled by upstream members.
result.label: K in QKD acronym

result.description: Fires on ' and' (rarely a comma or ' or') joining plural nouns in a list of technical or academic terms, such as "keys and foreign references". It stays silent on some common pairs like "shapes and sizes". Output pushes towards ' other' and ' their'.
result.label: Conjunction joining plural technical nouns

result.description: Fires on the word " due" in causal "due to" phrases, after a noun or verb describing an effect (e.g. "occurs due to", "largely due to"). Most members are detectors of " due" itself.
result.label: causal "due" in "due to"

result.description: Fires on function words (' the', 'or', ' which', ' prevent', ' either') in abstract explanatory prose defining concepts, such as probability, physics or economics, where a noun phrase or verb is expected next. Contrast shows ' the' often silent, so it is weak and mixed.
result.label: Function words in definitional academic prose

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (periods, ' f', ' seed', ' and', ' require') in academic-style text, often where a word beginning is expected next, e.g. 'f' continuing into 'fuzzy' or 'fairness'. Peaks are inconsistent and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered tokens predicting f-words

result.description: Fires on the word " high" (also High/highest) as a modifier before a noun, such as "high levels", "high-quality" or "high-speed". It pushes the next token towards "-", "standards", "levels" and "degree". Silent on the contrast text.
result.label: "high" as modifier before noun

result.description: Fires on the token ' method' when it starts a sentence as the subject, right after a full stop, in explanatory text about techniques. It is silent on 'this method' or 'elimination method'. It pushes towards suffixes like -ically and -ology.
result.label: Sentence-initial ' method' as subject

result.description: Fires on the token ' popular', most strongly in "rise in popularity" and "popular culture", and predicts suffixes like -ity, -ized and -izing. Upstream members are mostly ' popular' detectors from earlier layers.
result.label: ' popular' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ch' in "ever-ch(anging)", right after "ever-" or a similar hyphen prefix, and predicts "anging" or "alleng". It stays silent on 'ch' inside words like "eschewing" or "tech".
result.label: 'ch' in ever-changing

result.description: Fires on a place or scene noun right after "the" (streets, air, town, room, edge, side), in descriptive scene-setting prose. It seems to predict compound or location continuations such as yard, side, room, hall.
result.label: Setting noun after "the"

result.description: Fires on the word piece " impress" as the start of a word like impressive or impressions, predicting suffixes such as -ive, -ively, -ions. It is quieter when "impress" is a standalone verb.
result.label: " impress" word-start piece

result.description: Fires on verbs or verb pieces (shape, create, discover, reveal, -ing) in writing about characters and narrative, right before an expected object like "their inner/personal ...". The word ' with' peak is not reliable, since it stays silent in other topics.
result.label: Character-writing verb before 'their' object
'iffer' in "Differential"
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'iffer' in "D-iffer-ential", mainly in "Differential Equations" headings. It predicts continuations like 'ential'. Early-layer 'iffer' detectors drive it.

Fires on ' company' (weakly ' organization') after "the/a", in corporate-governance or workplace text about the organization itself. It pushes towards possessive 's, culture, executive. Silent in the contrast, which has no 'company' token.
result.label: ' company' as organization noun

result.description: Fires on adjectives or modifiers (complex, intricate, wider, diverse, distinct, shared) placed before an abstract noun in historical or political analysis prose, predicting nouns like politics, causes, circumstances. Silent on 'more complex' in an argument context.
result.label: Descriptive adjective before historical abstraction

result.description: Fires on ' Q' and ' statement' as logical or mathematical placeholder variables in modus ponens / conditional statement text ("if P implies Q", "conditional statement (if P"). Also weakly on a few word pieces. Circuit evidence is mixed.
result.label: Logic variable Q / conditional statement

result.description: Fires on "shape/shaping/shapes" and similar influence verbs (affect, influence, guide) where a subject like shared values or beliefs acts on people's behavior; predicts nouns like employees, behavior, members. Mostly in social/organizational text.
result.label: Shape/influence verb before behavior

result.description: Fires on the final noun of a plural or abstract subject noun phrase (science, systems, properties, resources, -ologies), where a plural verb like "are/have/include" is expected. Fires inconsistently; silent on "computer science" in some contexts.
result.label: Subject-noun-phrase head awaiting verb

result.description: Fires mainly on the ' U' token that starts "U.S." (United States), especially in historical or military text such as alliances and conflicts. Weaker peaks on a few other tokens (' offer', ' or', ' Sign') are mixed.
result.label: ' U' of U.S. in history

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' advoc' (advocate, advocating, advocacy), mostly in descriptions of ideologies or movements. Members are mainly ' advoc' detectors plus verb-stem pieces that precede "-ate".
result.label: ' advoc' word-stem detector

result.description: Fires on the word piece "ourse" in "discourse", as in "discourse analysis". It predicts "analysis" and similar words next. Many upstream members are also "ourse" detectors.
result.label: "ourse" in discourse

result.description: Fires on the word-piece 'com' (or ' Com') when it begins a longer word such as complement, comfortable, compress or comprehension. It pushes towards continuations like fort, bin, par, position. Silent on the word 'commas'.
result.label: 'com' word-initial piece

result.description: Fires on varied positions in scientific text where a word is likely to continue into "coll-" words (collapse, collide, colloid), e.g. ' col', ' L' in LTD, ' (' and '-'. Predicts 'lapsed', 'lide', 'der'. Mixed, low-faithfulness circuit.
result.label: Predicts coll- word continuations

result.description: Fires on the ' ent' piece that starts "entanglement" (also 'Ent', and some other quantum-physics pieces like 'istic') in quantum text, predicting 'ang'/'rop' continuations. Silent on ' ent' when entanglement follows other words without quantum context.
result.label: quantum ' ent' (entanglement) piece

result.description: Fires on the word piece " pro" when it begins a longer word split into pieces (probe, proton, progression, projections), mostly after "triode"/"planar"/"central" in probe text. Predicts continuations like "be", "ton", "gression".
result.label: " pro" word-start piece
'see' in 'overseeing'
result.description: Fires on the 'see' piece (and 'es' in 'oversees') inside 'oversee/overseeing', mostly in corporate-governance text about committees overseeing company matters. It needs the 'over' prefix, not standalone 'see'.
Fires on the period right after a section number (e.g. "### 4.", "2.1.") at the start of a numbered heading. It stays silent on sentence-ending periods after titles or prose.
result.label: Period after section number

result.description: Fires on mixed positions, often ' poll' (before 'ution') and function words like ' the'/' in' in economics or policy text, where a word-start piece is being predicted. Peaks are inconsistent, and the circuit is weak (low faithfulness).
result.label: Poll- word start, mixed function words

result.description: Fires on the word " social" (also " Social") as an adjective before a noun such as justice, issues, responsibility or structures. It pushes the next token toward words like justice, movements, inclusion and causes. Most members are earlier-layer detectors of " social".
result.label: ' social' adjective token

result.description: Fires on function words (the, of, to, as) right after "work" is being defined or described in physics text, where the next word would likely be work-related (done, performed, Work). Silent on the same words in other physics definitions not about work.
result.label: Function words after physics "work"

result.description: Fires on an abstract head noun (principle, factor, aspect, objective, challenge, advantage) right after an adjective like "key", "important", "main", "core" at the start of a statement. It predicts a following "is" or "lies" clause.
result.label: Abstract noun after "key/important"

result.description: Fires on minimizing adverbs like "merely", "just", "simply", "purely", mostly after "not"/"more than"/"is" in "not just X" style contrasts. It pushes toward a following article or noun phrase such as "a", "an", "another", "about".
result.label: Minimizing adverb 'merely/just/simply'

result.description: Fires on the token " depth" across contexts (tree depth, image depth estimation, water depth, depth and breadth). Members are mostly detectors of " depth" itself. Weakly also on "height" or "length" nouns.
result.label: ' depth' token detector

result.description: Fires on infinitive ' to' (also 'can', 'help') introducing a purpose clause in cooking and flavour text, such as "can be used to enhance". It stays quiet on 'to' after other verbs or in non-culinary contexts like "tuned to detect".
result.label: Purpose 'to' in culinary text

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' sp' (also ' Sp') at the start of a word split into pieces, such as span/spanning, spelling, spices, sp3. It pushes towards continuations like 'ans', 'anning' and 'anned'.
result.label: ' sp' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires mainly on mid-word pieces 'do' (in "redox") and 'ich' (in "Carmichael"), where a rare word is still being spelled out. Weak firing on some function words. Logits are mixed and unclear.
result.label: Mid-word 'do'/'ich' in rare words

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (function words, word-start fragments like ' prom', ' ev', ' cred', ' inaug') where the next token is likely a word continuation such as 'inence', 'ibility', 'idenced'. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Predicts word-continuation fragments

result.description: Fires on relative/linking pronouns (which, that, they) after a plural noun naming biological or chemical substances (metabolites, flavonoids, proteins), where a verb like act, serve, or confer comes next. Silent on some "which" clauses in other contexts.
result.label: Relative pronoun after plural science nouns

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' voc' (mostly before "abulary"), after adjectives or determiners like "new", "strong", "your". Predicts the continuation "ab". Rare weak firing on 'li' in "appliances".
result.label: ' voc' start of vocabulary

result.description: Fires on commas separating items in a bare list of technology or field names (e.g. "artificial intelligence, machine learning, analytics,"). It stays quiet on commas that end a clause or lead into a participle phrase such as ", leading to".
result.label: Comma in lists of tech fields

result.description: Fires on the document-start/boundary token (shown as ¶) when it comes after a short topic-title line in a list of headings, such as "Mathematics." or "Ecological Succession." It is silent on the first position and after long sentences. Next-token logits favor topic-like words.
result.label: Boundary token after topic-list titles

result.description: Fires on "found"/"finds" (also "find", "finding") when a non-human subject such as a concept, technique, or instrument "has found" its way, use, or place. Predicts words like "expression", "its", "new", "use", "resonance".
result.label: 'found' as 'found its way/use'

result.description: Fires on the auxiliary ' has'/' have' after a noun subject in essay-style text about influence or impact, where a present-perfect verb like "not only inspired" follows. Silent on "geology has become" in a historical sentence.
result.label: has/have before "not only" perfect

result.description: Fires on the verb or preposition after "a branch of physics/science that..." (studies, deals with, focuses on, involves), where the next word is the subject matter, especially fluids and flow. Silent on ordinary "with" in other uses.
result.label: Field-definition verb before subject matter

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' cru' when it begins "crucial", mostly after "is" in phrases like "X is crucial for/to". Many upstream members are themselves ' cru' detectors from earlier layers.
result.label: ' cru' in "crucial"

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ar' completing "Laminar" in fluid-dynamics text (laminar flow). Weak activations on a few function words elsewhere. Members include 'ar' detectors and fluid/flow-word detectors.
result.label: 'ar' in "laminar" (flow)

result.description: Fires on the noun ending a list or phrase of rules (standards, requirements, regulations, laws) in compliance and regulatory text, where a following word like "set" or "specified" is expected. Silent on some "standards" in other phrasings.
result.label: Regulatory rule nouns in compliance text
'become' predicting evolving significance
result.description: Fires on ' become/becoming/became' (occasionally 'as', 'into') when a subject such as festivals is described as turning into something increasingly significant. Silent on 'become' in a plain comparative ("areas become more closely linked"). Predicts adjectives like cultural, significant, global.

Fires on possessive markers (apostrophe, 's) after individual/user/person nouns, and on "individual"/"own", in ethics and rights text, where the next word is likely a right or trait like autonomy, rights, liberty or privacy. Silent on "Today's" and "it's".
result.label: Possessive of individual, then rights

result.description: Fires on word pieces like ' int' (before "ake", as in water/energy intake), 'ites' in "satellites", and ' payload'. Mostly the ' int' piece in intake-type contexts, with a few other scattered tokens. Predicts "ake".
result.label: ' int' of intake, satellites

result.description: Fires on plural subject nouns like ' groups' (also -isms, -s) that are about to take a plural verb, e.g. "various ethnic groups coexist/live". Silent when the noun is followed by a period or ends a phrase after "between/among".
result.label: Plural subject noun awaiting verb

result.description: Fires on nouns meaning a case or circumstance (scenarios, situations, situation, scenario), mostly after adjectives like hypothetical, possible or worst-case. It pushes toward "where" or "involving" as the next word.
result.label: scenario/situation nouns before "where"

result.description: Fires on "light" (and sunlight, light rays, radiation) in physics or optics-style text about light, scattering and rays. Silent on sound wave text. Predicts continuations like cast, filtered, ray, dim.
result.label: light as physical phenomenon

result.description: Fires on list separators (commas, "and", "or", "),") inside lists of causes or problems like errors, failures and data corruption, where a further negative item (lack of, poor, incorrect) is expected next. Silent on "and" in neutral lists.
result.label: List separators in cause-of-error lists

result.description: Fires on adjectives like cultural, unique, distinct, diverse, and "genetic" that modify a following noun in texts about diversity of societies or species. It predicts nouns like identities, characteristics, traditions, attributes.
result.label: Diversity adjectives before attribute nouns

result.description: Fires on nationality or regional adjectives (Indian, Chinese, European, Arab) used as modifiers before a noun like mathematics, science, or civilization, mostly in history-of-science text. It predicts nouns such as society, history, intellectual.
result.label: Nationality adjective before culture noun

result.description: Fires on the noun "relationships" (also "connections", "-hips" in "partnerships", "relations") when it is the head noun of a phrase about people or entities. It pushes the next token toward "between", "with" or "among".
result.label: relationships / connections noun

result.description: Fires on "crucial", "essential" or "critical" when used as a predicate adjective after "is/are" (e.g. "precision is crucial for…"), anticipating a following "for/to". Silent on attributive uses like "an essential role" or "essential depth cues".
result.label: Predicative "crucial/essential" adjective

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ious' completing "harmonious" (weaker on "synergistic", "symbiotic"). It predicts nouns of balance or blending such as "blend", "balance", "proportion" and "combinations".
result.label: harmon-ious suffix

result.description: Fires on ' intellectual' (also ' cultural') as an adjective in Renaissance-style descriptions of a period of intellectual, artistic and cultural flourishing, e.g. "a period of intellectual revival". Silent on some other uses, such as "literary and intellectual traditions".
result.label: intellectual in period-of-flourishing phrases

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments (e.g. ' dec' before 'isions', 'p' in Responsibility) and some function words where a word continuation suffix such as 'isions' or 'ons' is expected. Mixed peaks; weak consistency.
result.label: Incomplete word-piece awaiting suffix

result.description: Fires on the first piece of a split verb stem (unders-, ill-, enh-, im-, enc-, fost-) in academic-style prose, right where a verb like "underscores" or "illuminates" is about to be completed. It predicts the suffix, such as -ributes, -poses or -uminate.
result.label: Verb-stem fragment before suffix

result.description: Fires on function words like " involves", " to", " of" in explanatory text defining paraphrasing (or similar skills like listening), where the next word is likely a verb describing the process, such as restating in original words. Silent on " involves" in other topics.
result.label: Paraphrasing definition connectors

result.description: Fires mostly on the mid-word piece 'ere' in "cerebrum/cerebellum/cerebral", with weaker firing on other mid-word fragments such as 'ide' and 'cer'. Members are detectors of 'ere' fragments.
result.label: 'ere' inside cerebrum

result.description: Fires on function words and verbs like "of", "understanding", "understand" in art-criticism text about analyzing or interpreting artworks and artistic intent, where the next word is likely art-related (works, art, texts). Silent on "of" in generic social-science text.
result.label: Art criticism interpretation connectives

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' ref' when it starts a word like refining, refinery, refinement, refraction or reflexive, and pushes the next token toward continuations such as 'in', 'ining' and 'ract'. Most windows are about metal or petroleum processing.
result.label: ' ref' word-start piece (refining)

result.description: Fires mainly on the 'ynast' piece in "Dynasty" after a Chinese dynasty name (Shang, Zhou, Tang, Song, Yuan), with weaker firing on scattered word pieces and commas. Circuit is low-faithfulness and mixed.
result.label: Dynasty 'ynast' word piece

result.description: Fires on word pieces 'arith', 'Cos'/'cos', 'yth' that are the start of a word continuing with "-mic"/"-m(s)" (logarithmic, cosmic, rhythm). Predicts the "mic/ms/m" continuation.
result.label: Word piece before -mic/-ms ending

result.description: Fires mostly on ' rock' and other words in geology/erosion/sediment passages (transport, depositional, the), where the next word is likely a geological process or surface term. Members are erosion, glacier and sediment detectors.
result.label: Rock in erosion/sediment geology text

result.description: Fires on intensifying adverbs (-ly, significantly, greatly, directly) placed before a verb like affect, impact, influence, determine, predicting such verbs next. Silent on -ly adverbs in other positions (chiefly, markedly evolved).
result.label: Adverb before affect/influence verb

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'ater' piece in "catering"/"caterers" and "extraterrestrial", plus scattered words like "organ", "to", "include" and "purchase". Mixed evidence; the 'ater' fragment is the main trigger, and the 'catering to' phrase is the clearest context.
result.label: 'ater' in catering / extraterrestrial

result.description: Fires on plural nouns for physical entities (objects, atoms, electrons, particles) in physics/science explanations, often as the subject or object of a motion or arrangement description. Silent on abstract physics terms like phonon mode.
result.label: Plural physical-entity nouns in physics

result.description: Fires on function words (of, that, the, commas) in software development/engineering text, where the next word is likely a software term like bug, refactor or deployment. Silent on the same words in non-software contexts such as finance or history.
result.label: Function words in software-engineering text

result.description: Fires mostly on the word-start piece ' vers' (as in versatile/versatility) and similar incomplete word beginnings like ' vol', ' u' (ubiquitous), 'Aut'. It predicts continuations such as 'atile' and 'at'. Weaker, mixed cases exist.
result.label: ' vers' fragment predicting 'atile'

result.description: Fires on function words (of, in, with, celebrated, only) in text about knights, nobles, chivalry and medieval courts, where the next word is likely to be an honor/grandeur-type noun. Silent on 'of' in unrelated phrases like 'coat of arms' or 'of course'.
result.label: Function words in chivalry/nobility text

result.description: Fires on varied function words and nouns (to, that, this, these, analysis, patterns) in analytical essay prose, often where an abstract noun like "story" or "context" is expected next. Members mostly relate to writing, narrative and plot. Mixed evidence.
result.label: Analytical prose slot before abstract noun

result.description: Fires on commas and "and"/"or" separating items in a list of abstract positive qualities or skills (honesty, passion, authenticity, confidence), predicting another such quality noun next (dedication, commitment, precision).
result.label: Separators in lists of virtues

result.description: Fires on an opening parenthesis (or dash/bracket) after a term in linguistics or language-study text, where a gloss, example or abbreviation follows. It stays silent on parentheses in other topics, such as names or PDE. Logits favour linguistic words.
result.label: Parenthesis in linguistics text

result.description: Fires on the word " fair" (fairness, fair trade, fair treatment), mostly in ethics or economics text. It predicts suffixes like "ness" or "y". Members are mostly earlier " fair" and "equitable" detectors.
result.label: ' fair' token detector

result.description: Fires on commas and conjunctions (and, or, as well as) in lists of nouns about food, ingredients and production processes, where another noun like processes, components or finished items is expected next. Silent on some commas in other clause types.
result.label: List separators in food/process lists

result.description: Fires on ' as' (also 'became', 'a', 'an') after a subject when the word introduces the role or status it takes on, as in "emerged as", "serving as", "radio became an". Silent on "seen as", "as well as", and temporal "as".
result.label: Role-predicate 'as/became' after subject

result.description: Fires on the noun " topic" (also " theme", " topics") when it is the object of a phrase like "choose the right topic" or "main topics". Upstream members are mostly topic/theme/subject detectors. Predicts words like "discussed" and "sentence".
result.label: topic / theme noun detector

result.description: Fires on the final noun or word piece of academic-activity phrases after a scholarly modifier, e.g. "scientific inquiry", "scientific exploration", "philosophical discourse", "scientific discovery", "evolutionary research". Predicts continuations like "conducted".
result.label: Scholarly inquiry/research noun after field adjective

result.description: Fires on the ending piece ('ve', 'ves', 'ive') of the verb "delve" (also dive/venture-like verbs), predicting "deeper"/"into". Silent on contractions like "we've" and on "convection".
result.label: "delve" verb ending piece

result.description: Fires on " Global" as the first word of a line or heading in a list of course or topic titles (e.g. "Global Supply Chains"). Weak on lowercase "global" mid-sentence. Pushes toward "Position", "supply", "Navigation".
result.label: Global as heading-initial word

result.description: Fires on the document-boundary token (shown as ¶ / <s>) that separates short, title-like or topical academic lines, right after a sentence or heading ends and a new document starts. Silent on ordinary mid-text tokens.
result.label: Document-start boundary token

result.description: Fires on "cial" completing "Financial" (and on " financial") in finance contexts, predicting finance nouns like instruments, institutions, products, reporting. Silent on "cial" in "crucial".
result.label: Financial word piece, finance nouns next

result.description: Fires on the token ' advantage' when it is the stem of "advantageous" (e.g. "can be advantage|ous"), pushing the next token toward the suffix "ous". It is weak on plain "advantage"/"disadvantage".
result.label: advantage- stem before -ous

result.description: Fires on the prefix " meta" (and "Meta") as a word-start piece, as in meta-analysis, meta-narrative, metafiction. It predicts continuations like "analysis" and "comment". Upstream members mostly detect " meta" itself.
result.label: meta- prefix token
Artificial Intelligence 'elligence' piece
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'elligence' completing "Artificial Intelligence", often in titles and headings. Weakly on ' intelligence' after "artificial". Silent on generic technology text without that phrase.

Fires on function words (of, the, with, both, -level) in workplace motivation and organizational psychology text, especially where a noun like attachment, commitment or satisfaction is likely next. It is silent on 'of' in generic non-psychology contexts.
result.label: Function words in organizational psychology text

result.description: Fires on the newline/document-boundary token (shown as ¶) that follows a short topic-title line in a list of terse headings (e.g. "Immunology.¶"), where a new heading or section begins. Silent on a document-initial ¶.
result.label: Newline after list-of-topics heading

result.description: Fires on prepositions or verbs like "for", "of", "towards", "developing" that come before a goal or object in quantum computing and technology text (e.g. "paving the way for"). It is silent on "for" in many similar contexts, and the logits favour "fault", "stabil", "practical".
result.label: Quantum-computing prepositions before technical goals

result.description: Fires on the pronoun " we" (also "We") as the subject starting a new clause or sentence in expository text, often after a period or comma. It stays quiet when "we" follows "where" or "in which" in a relative clause.
result.label: Clause-initial "we" in exposition

result.description: Fires on the verb ' add' (also adds/adding) in the sense of contributing a quality, as in "can add depth/color/excitement". Members are mostly detectors of 'add' forms. Predicts nouns like depth or character.
result.label: 'add' as contributing a quality

result.description: Fires on word-start pieces 'under' (e.g. thunderstorm split as th|under, 'under the weather') and ' infrastr' (before 'ucture'), where a longer word continues. Logits favour word-completing suffixes.
result.label: 'under' and 'infrastr' word-pieces

result.description: Fires on verbs and prepositions that introduce an object of analysis or understanding, such as "insight into", "understanding", "examine", "analyze" and "explain", in abstract mathematical text. It predicts nouns like "relationships", "how" and "properties".
result.label: Insight-into / understanding in math text
' rh' word-start piece (rhythm, rhyme)
result.description: Fires on the word piece ' rh' at the start of words like rhythm, rhyme and rhetoric, and pushes the next token towards continuations like 'ythm' and 'yme'. Upstream members are mostly ' rh' detectors across earlier layers.

Fires on words inside title-like topic phrases (e.g. "Understanding Digital Palette", "Producing a Weather Map"), in academic or course-style headings. It predicts a following subject noun such as book, record or Audio. Peaks are mixed.
result.label: Title-phrase words predicting subject nouns

result.description: Fires on the noun ending a second object after "combine/blend/merge X with [domain] NOUN" (skill, principles, commentary, motifs), where a blended-domains phrase is being completed. Pushes toward verbs like "to/creates". Peaks are mixed.
result.label: Noun completing "blend X with Y" phrase

result.description: Fires on the word " contributions" (also " contribution" and "contributors"), mostly where someone's or something's contributions are discussed. It predicts " to" or "towards" next. Members are mostly detectors of the same word.
result.label: ' contributions' token detector

result.description: Fires on the pronoun " we" as a clause subject, usually after a comma or sentence break in expository text. It predicts a following verb such as want, shall, aim or ensure. It stays silent on "we" in a relative clause or at the very start of a text.
result.label: Subject pronoun " we" before verb

result.description: Fires on commas separating items in a list of cultural elements (customs, languages, architecture, crafts, religion), where another cultural-domain item is expected next. Silent on commas in ordinary clauses or non-list uses.
result.label: Commas in cultural-element lists

result.description: Fires on scattered word-start or mid-word pieces ('1' in a year, 'co' of cooperation, ' between') in text about treaties and diplomacy, such as the Helsinki Accords. Peaks are mixed, and the same '1' stays silent in other year contexts.
result.label: Diplomacy-text mixed pieces (1, co, between)

result.description: Fires on determiners (' the', ' its', ' a') that begin a second or coordinated noun phrase in descriptive praise of a style or work, e.g. "and the allure of", "characterized by its elegance". Predicts abstract qualities like clarity, sense, desire.
result.label: Determiner before abstract quality noun

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' em' when it is the start of "emissions", mostly after "greenhouse gas" or "carbon", and predicts "issions". Weakly fires on other em- words such as embody and empathy.
result.label: ' em' before -issions

result.description: Fires on function words and punctuation (commas, ' the', ' of') in abstract expository text about epistemology, belief systems and expert systems, where an analysis-type noun may come next. Peaks are scattered; the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words in abstract theory text

result.description: Fires on function words (of, the, about, include, considers) in explanatory text about survival analysis and time-to-event statistics, where the next word would be a term like survival, censoring, lifetime or death. Silent on 'of' in other statistical phrases.
result.label: Function words before survival-analysis terms

result.description: Fires on plural-variety determiners (" different", " multiple", " various") placed before a plural noun, especially in technical text about combining or distributing data, views or sources. Predicts nouns like views, sources, modal.
result.label: different/multiple/various before plural noun

result.description: Fires on " in" introducing a setting or context in communication/tone-in-situations text, especially "such as in-person meetings" or "in Western cultures". Predicts communication nouns like emails, written, customer. Silent on " in" in other topics.
result.label: " in" for communication settings

result.description: Fires on the possessive 's after the generic pronoun "one" (one's own ...), predicting " own" or "self". It stays silent on 's after "it", nouns like "world" or "speaker", and other non-"one" contexts.
result.label: possessive 's after "one"

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ative' in "collabor-ative" (also cooper-ative), predicting nouns like efforts, problem, spirit. Silent on 'ative' in innovative, narrative, participative.
result.label: collaborative suffix 'ative'

result.description: Fires mostly on the suffix "al" in "disposal" (also "ing", " prior", " increasing"), where the next word is likely a noun like "methods" or "site". Silent on "al" in other words like "portrayal" or "institutional".
result.label: "disposal" suffix 'al'

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ural' completing "architectural" (after "architect"). It stays silent on 'ural' in "structural". Predicts nouns like styles, designs, wonders, projects.
result.label: 'ural' in "architectural"

result.description: Fires on function words (of, the, their, an) right after verbs like measure/evaluate/assess in text about measuring innovation, predicting "innov(ation)" next. Silent on 'of' in other business contexts.
result.label: Function word before predicted 'innovation'

result.description: Fires on function words and adjectives (' the', ' to', ' essential', 'cial') in sentences saying something is crucial or contributes to organizational functioning, especially in organizational behavior text. It stays silent on many ' the' tokens elsewhere. Predicts words like 'formal', 'organiz', 'operation'.
result.label: Organizational-contribution phrasing, 'the' slot

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' une' (start of "unequal", "uneven") and pushes the next token toward 'qual', 'ven', 'quality'. Upstream members are mostly ' une' detectors; weak activation elsewhere.
result.label: ' une' prefix before qual/ven

result.description: Fires on an apostrophe that comes right after sentence-ending punctuation (a period) and starts a new sentence or clause, as in ".'s important" or ".'t". It stays silent on possessive or contraction apostrophes attached to a word, such as "one's" or "someone's".
result.label: Apostrophe after sentence-final period

result.description: Fires on the piece "inal" in "marginal" (marginal utility/cost/analysis), in economics text. It stays silent on "inal" in "seminal", so it needs the "marg" prefix. Predicts "-ized"/"utility"-type continuations.
result.label: "inal" in "marginal" (economics)
Computing noun modifier before technical noun
result.description: Fires on a noun used as a modifier in computing/networking text (process, system, device, frame, network, command), where another technical noun is expected next (timeout, ports, tables, interrupt). Silent on 'process' in general business or engineering text.

Fires on abstract head nouns (area, aspect, topic, element) right after an evaluative adjective like crucial, critical, important, significant, in a "has become a crucial area of..." predicate. Predicts " of". Silent after "this area".
result.label: Head noun after "crucial/important" adjective

result.description: Fires on the word "digital"/"Digital" (any case), as in digital printmaking, digital art, digital media. Upstream members are mostly earlier-layer detectors of the same word. Silent on unrelated text such as music streaming.
result.label: Digital token detector

result.description: Fires on function words (the, comma, and, of) in technical text about chemical, biological or engineering processes, where the next word is likely a chemistry or engineering term. Silent on the same words in other contexts.
result.label: Function words in chemical engineering text

result.description: Fires on " only" in the "not only" construction, right after "not" with a verb expected next (enabled, enriches, illustrated). Predicts verbs like "advanced", "improved", "enhance". Silent in other contexts.
result.label: "not only" correlative 'only'

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' fost' as the start of "foster/fosters/fostering", mostly in abstract essay text about communication or collaboration. It predicts the suffix (er, ers, ered). It is silent on some ' fost' tokens, notably "fostering" after "also" or "in".
result.label: ' fost' start of foster

result.description: Fires on scattered connective tokens (' and', commas, ' including', 'och') in academic or technical prose, often linguistics or music. Peaks are mixed and inconsistent. The contrast shows ' and' in plain lists stays silent.
result.label: Connectives in academic linguistics prose

result.description: Fires on ' that' as a relative pronoun right after an abstract noun describing a skill, tool, technique or art form ("a powerful tool that can..."). Silent on demonstrative or complementizer 'that' (emphasize that, with that person).
result.label: Relative 'that' after skill/tool noun

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly " of", also possessive "s", "possess") in abstract essays on nature, art, spirituality and the sublime, where the next word is likely a lofty noun (inspiration, spiritual, sacred). Silent on " of" in other, more mundane constructions.
result.label: "of" before lofty abstract nouns

result.description: Fires on commas, "as well as", "and" and "),". These separators fall inside lists of infrastructure types (transit, water, sewage, electricity), where the next item is likely communication, telecom or utilities. Silent on commas after "networks" in other contexts.
result.label: Infrastructure list separators

result.description: Fires on the 'AL' piece in the acronym SALT (Strategic Arms Limitation Talks), after "(S", in Cold War arms-control text. It pushes the next token toward 'T'.
result.label: AL in SALT acronym

result.description: Fires mostly on a hyphen in compound words, strongest in "step-growth" after "step" or "chain" in polymer text, predicting a word-piece continuation. Also fires weakly on function words like "of", "the", "and". Silent on other hyphens like "higher-", "non-".
result.label: Hyphen in step-growth compounds

result.description: Fires mainly on the word piece ' fir' when it begins "firms" (economics text), predicting 'ms'. Also weakly fires on 'iz' in "Organizational" and on ' the' after "understanding". The circuit is mostly 'fir' detectors.
result.label: "fir" before "ms" (firms)

result.description: Fires mid-word on incomplete word pieces in topic or heading lists, mainly 'chni' in "Techniques", plus ' Indust' (Industrial) and ' relief'/' appro'. It seems to predict a suffix completing the word (ries, ry, ction).
result.label: Word-fragment in heading lists

result.description: Fires on mixed function words (and, in, to, may, can, providing) in technical or scientific expository prose, after a clause where a continuation follows. It is silent on many ' and' tokens in lists. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Function words in technical prose

result.description: Fires on a passive past participle (established, created, formed, initiated, attained, reached) right after "is/are/be", completing a passive verb. Silent when "established" is an adjective after "with/to".
result.label: Passive participle after auxiliary

result.description: Fires on the word piece "agement" completing "engagement", mostly in marketing or business metrics contexts (customer, audience, community engagement). It predicts nouns like metrics, strategies, levels and tactics.
result.label: "engagement" suffix 'agement'

result.description: Fires on function words (for, and, offer, of, to) in technology/materials text, right before a predicted benefit or improved-performance word like "faster", "longer", "higher", "dens(ity)". Silent on many other uses of " for".
result.label: Function words before performance-benefit terms

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' the', ' of', ' should') and word pieces mid-phrase, where the next word is open. The peaks share no clear token or construction, and the same ' the' stays silent in the contrast. The evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words, unclear

result.description: Fires on a comma that follows a full stop, where a sentence-ending period is immediately followed by a comma and a new fragment or list item starts. It stays silent on ordinary mid-sentence commas after a clause or phrase.
result.label: Comma right after a period

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'enger' piece in "messenger" (messenger RNA) in molecular biology text. It also fires weakly on ' mathematical' in Egyptian papyrus text and on a few other tokens. Members include 'enger' detectors and biology/gene-expression context.
result.label: 'enger' in messenger (RNA)

result.description: Fires on ' is'/' are' right after a plural or abstract subject noun phrase in academic/scientific text (e.g. "research on X is", "studies are"), where a progressive or ongoing predicate comes next (continuing, focused, evolving). Silent on other 'is' uses.
result.label: Copula after scientific subject noun

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' ur' when it begins a longer word, mainly "urgency" in "urgency and importance" task-prioritization text. Predicts continuations like "gency". Members are mostly ' ur' detectors plus other word-start fragment detectors.
result.label: ' ur' start of 'urgency'

result.description: Fires on ' the' after "X is" or "refers to" in a definitional sentence about an abstract concept (cohesion, rhythm, motivation), anticipating an abstract noun like "process", "basis", "foundation". Silent on some similar "is the" cases.
result.label: 'the' in concept definitions

result.description: Fires on a hyphen or en dash joining a noun or compound's first part to a following word, as in "problem-", "data-" or "concept-to-operation-". It is silent on hyphens after "cross", "20th" or "fiberglass", and on a hyphen at text start. Boosts next-token words like making, building and testing.
result.label: Hyphen in noun compounds

result.description: Fires on commas and function words (and, in, of, how) in abstract expository text about probability, statistics and math, mid-sentence where a technical term should follow. Mixed peaks; members mostly push probability-related continuations. Weak, inconsistent.
result.label: Function words in probability/math exposition

result.description: Fires on function words (and, on, with, -ized) in passages about the Protestant work ethic, where "emphasis/emphasized hard work, frugality" is being listed. It stays silent on 'and' in other lists, so it appears tied to this passage's theme.
result.label: Emphasis on hard work, frugality

result.description: Fires on the space or dash token right before a year's digits in ancient Greek philosophy dates (e.g. "Socrates (470-399", "circa 470"), where the next token is a digit. It stays quiet on similar year spaces in other history contexts.
result.label: Year-start separator in ancient Greek dates

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' simultane' (simultaneity, simultaneous), mostly in physics/relativity text. It predicts suffix continuations like -ity/-ous, as shown by members that detect similar stems (continu, proxim, autonom).
result.label: ' simultane' word-stem before suffix

result.description: Fires on function words and connectors (' multiple', ' that', ' on', ' with', 'uting') in descriptions of memory interleaving, spreading addresses across memory banks. Silent on ' multiple' in other computing contexts. Logits favor '-ade/-ading' endings, which look unrelated.
result.label: Memory interleaving spread connectors

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' trans' (start of a split word), strongest in 'phase trans-' before 'itions'. Weaker on other trans- words like transcends, transpiration, Fourier Transform. Predicts continuations such as 'itions', 'fers', 'itional'.
result.label: ' trans' prefix, phase transitions

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ptic' in "haptic" (also 'ic' in "Haptic"), in text about haptic feedback and technology. It predicts continuations like glove, feedback and correction. The contrast text on interactive environments stays silent.
result.label: haptic word piece 'ptic'

result.description: Fires on ' into' right after a verb of change or development (evolved into, expanded into, turn into), where the next word names the resulting form. Silent on ' into' after nouns like "research into" or "insight into", or after "integrating into".
result.label: ' into' after evolve/transform verbs

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (mostly ' the', also ' for', ' like') and word pieces in mathematical/technical text, e.g. Riemann hypothesis, induction, algebra. Silent on ' the' in writing/literary text. Evidence is mixed and weak.
result.label: ' the' in mathematical text

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' ded' at the start of "deductive", and on ' Cont' before "inuous" in tense names. Predicts continuation pieces like 'uct' and 'inu'. Mostly a detector of these split word beginnings.
result.label: ' ded' / ' Cont' word-start pieces

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' harm' when it begins "harmony" or "harmonious" (e.g. "visual harmony", "culinary harmony"), and predicts continuations like 'ony'. It stays silent on ' harm' in "harmonizing" after a verb.
result.label: ' harm' start of harmony

result.description: Fires on the final piece of "photosynthesis" (' thesis' after 'photosyn'), and less on 'iration' in "respiration", in biology text on plant metabolism. Silent on other biology topic lists.
result.label: photosynthesis / respiration word ending

result.description: Fires on a comma right after a coordinated pair of concepts ("X and Y,") in academic-style text, where a clause like "which are fundamental/essential" or "respectively" follows. Predicts words like both, two, respectively.
result.label: Comma after paired concepts "X and Y,"

result.description: Fires on 'stone' in 'cornerstone' when used figuratively as a foundational concept ("a cornerstone of theory"). Weakly on similar words like 'staple'. Predicts 'of', 'in', 'upon' next.
result.label: cornerstone as foundational concept

result.description: Fires on the noun " use" in "the use of" after "involves/requires/necessitates the", in expository text about methods. Silent when "use" is a verb ("we use", "to use"). Predicts " of".
result.label: Noun "use" in "the use of"

result.description: Fires on "such as" / "like" / "including" introducing examples after "civilizations" or ancient societies, predicting a named ancient culture next (Greece, Mesopotamia, Egypt). Silent on "such as" after other nouns (systems, services, workers).
result.label: "such as" before ancient civilizations

result.description: Fires on list-introducing words ("including", "such as", "include", commas) right after "environmental factors" in biology text about plant or microbial growth. It predicts the factors that follow, such as temperature, light exposure, availability and nutrients.
result.label: Introducing environmental factor lists

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ance' (also 'ances', 'ening') completing the verb "enhance" (or heighten) in writing/literature text, predicting an object like "the richness". Silent on 'ance' in nouns such as resonance or substance.
result.label: enh-ance verb suffix

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments that begin a known multi-piece name or term, mainly ' A' in "Middle Ages" and ' Haw' in "Hawking", also ' Bol' and ' Dar'. It predicts the continuation piece (ges, king, tons).
result.label: Name-start fragments (Middle A|ges, Haw|king)

result.description: Fires mainly on 'une' inside "cuneiform" (c-une-iform) and on the hyphen in "COVID-19", mid-word or mid-compound pieces where a specific completion follows. Silent on 'une' in "lune-isform", a different word.
result.label: cuneiform 'une' and COVID- hyphen

result.description: Fires on ' of' right after "the beginning/start/genesis" when describing an event marking the start of an era or development. Silent on ' of' after other nouns like "introduction", "understanding", "advantage", "Age". Predicts a, an, significant.
result.label: "beginning of" in era-marking phrases

result.description: Fires on function words (" of", " the", " how") right after measurement or quantifying words (measurement of, measures the, quantifies how), predicting magnitude nouns like distance, intensity, dispersion. Silent on other " of" phrases such as "in terms of" or "course of".
result.label: Function word after measuring verbs

result.description: Fires on names of software tools, languages and libraries (Jenkins, Python, Perl, GitHub, MySQL, PyTorch pieces) inside lists of developer tools. Silent on generic continuous-integration prose. Boosts next tokens like library/libraries.
result.label: Software tool and language names

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' ref' when it begins a word like refinement, refining, reflexive or refraction, mostly after "the" or "and". It predicts continuations such as 'in', 'lections' and 'ined'. It is silent on 'reflecting'.
result.label: ' ref' word-start (refinement)

result.description: Fires on the word "key" (key/Key), mostly in cryptography text such as "symmetric key", "asymmetric key", "key distribution". It also fires more weakly on "key factor". Members detect "key" and encryption context.
result.label: "key" in cryptography

result.description: Fires on ' is' after a long abstract noun-phrase subject (e.g. "monitoring of pH levels", "effective scheduling"), in formal expository text, where an evaluative predicate like "essential" is expected. Silent on short subjects or "goal is".
result.label: ' is' after abstract nominal subject

result.description: Fires on the head noun (behavior, relationships, trade, plural endings) that is the object of "impact/influence/affect", where an adverb or outcome word like "significantly" or "outcome" would come next. It is silent on "behavior" in other constructions.
result.label: Object noun after impact/influence verbs

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and connectors (to, with, of, for, or, near, clear) in expository text, where a noun phrase is expected next. No dominant token; the contrast shows it silent on many ' to' uses.
result.label: Scattered connectors before noun phrase

result.description: Fires on verbs of bringing about or promoting (create, creating, promote, achieve, foster) in urban planning text, where the next word is likely a desirable urban quality like mixed-use, compact or walkable. Silent on 'create' in a non-urban employment context.
result.label: Urban-planning 'create/promote' verbs

result.description: Fires on mixed function words and fragments (mostly ' of', also 'not', ' new', ' network') in technical or academic prose, often where a technical term such as a language or science word comes next. Peaks are inconsistent, and ' of' is often silent.
result.label: Scattered ' of' in technical prose

result.description: Fires on connectors (and, in, including, commas) in lists of application domains for AI/technology, where the next item is a sector like health, security, retail, or autonomous systems. Silent on 'and' in generic lists of abstract nouns.
result.label: Connectors before application-domain lists

result.description: Fires on the word piece "our" in "contour", mostly in topographic map and contour line text. Members also detect "our" in other words (outsourcing, Gourmet), and the target predicts "line", "lines" and similar next.
result.label: "our" in "contour"

result.description: Fires on verbs and linking words (-ing, 'ensuring', 'for', 'keeping', 'empowers') that come before an object of benefit or outcome in business and IT-strategy writing, for example 'critical for ensuring the sustained...'. It is silent on many other -ing endings.
result.label: Business purpose verbs: ensuring, for

result.description: Fires on ' is' right after an abstract noun-phrase subject (e.g. "Its beauty is", "the diversity of styles and loops is"), where the next word is likely an evaluative or predicate word. Silent after pronouns, "that", or "there".
result.label: ' is' after abstract noun subject

result.description: Fires most on ' relativ' (relativity/relativistic) in physics-style text, but also weakly on scattered function words like ' of' and ' the'. It stays silent on ' relativ' in moral/cultural relativism. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is unfaithful.
result.label: ' relativ' in physics, plus scattered ' of'

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and verb pieces (it in "exhibit", of, between, like, convey, capture) in explanatory text on photography, physics and science, where a noun phrase is expected next. Peaks are inconsistent; evidence is mixed.
result.label: Mixed function words in science/photography text

result.description: Fires on the 'ier' piece completing "Le Chatelier", right before "'s Principle". It is silent on a lowercase "chatelier" in a different context. It pushes the next token towards " Princi".
result.label: 'ier' in Le Chatelier

result.description: Fires on 'ic' completing "Strategic", strongest in title-like headings at document start (e.g. "Strategic Resource Allocation"). Weaker mid-sentence, and silent on 'ic' in other words or some mid-sentence "strategic" uses.
result.label: 'ic' in "Strategic" headings

result.description: Fires on a comma (or dash) right after "all" or a sentence-initial adverb like "after all," or "sometimes,". Members detect "all" plus quantifier-like continuations. Silent on commas elsewhere, e.g. after clauses.
result.label: Comma after "all" / "after all"

result.description: Fires mainly on the word-piece " Ent" at the start of "Entropy" or "Entanglement", especially in headings or at the start of a sentence. Members are mostly Ent/ent detectors. Weak activity elsewhere on function words.
result.label: Ent- piece (Entropy/Entanglement)

result.description: Fires on connectors (and, comma, 's, their) right after "credibility"/"trustworthiness" in explanations of ethos in rhetoric, where the next word is likely authority, trust, character or credentials. Silent on 'and' in other persuasion text.
result.label: Ethos credibility list connectors

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (plural endings, commas, 'and', 'for', 'years', 'monument') in abstract academic or expository prose about environment, science and society. Peaks are inconsistent, with no single token or construction. The logits are unclear.
result.label: Scattered tokens in expository prose

result.description: Fires on scattered function and verb tokens (the, exposed, improve, when, to) in technical chemistry, materials and surface-science text, often where a chemistry-related noun is expected next. Peaks are mixed and weak; the circuit is low-faithfulness.
result.label: Chemistry/materials text, mixed function words

result.description: Fires on varied function words and word pieces (' of', ',', 'ic', 'ing', ' and', ' into') in academic or health/science prose, where the next word is open. It stays silent on ' of' in computer-science text. Evidence is mixed and the circuit's faithfulness is low.
result.label: Function words in academic health prose

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' des' (also ' ent') when it begins a longer word such as desperately, desires, desirable, and predicts continuations like -ire, -irable, -perate. Mostly silent elsewhere.
result.label: ' des' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' whe' (mostly the start of "wheat", e.g. in lists of crops), predicting the continuation "at". A few weak firings occur on commas and 'of'.
result.label: ' whe' piece before "at" (wheat)

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and mid-phrase tokens (and, to, the, be, current, match) in technical or expository prose, where the next word is a technical noun or verb. Peaks are inconsistent; the evidence is mixed and weak.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' expl' (or 'pl' after 'Ex') when it begins the word "exploration"/"explorers", predicting continuations like 'oration', 'orer', 'oring'. Mostly in history/Age of Exploration text.
result.label: expl- start of exploration

result.description: Fires on the word ' utility', most strongly in economics or utilitarian-theory text (utility of consumption, marginal utility). It is weaker in the plain 'usefulness' sense. Upstream members are mostly earlier-layer detectors of the same token.
result.label: ' utility' token (economics sense)

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verbs (with, from, as, involves, include, addresses) that follow a technical subject in definitional academic text and introduce what it involves or deals with. Peaks are scattered and weakly consistent. Silent on "benefits from".
result.label: Connector after technical topic noun

result.description: Fires on the word " failure" (rarely " fail"), mostly in engineering and fatigue-analysis text, where it is followed by "modes" or similar. Upstream members are failure-token detectors plus fatigue, loading and stress context.
result.label: ' failure' token, engineering fatigue context

result.description: Fires on "demonstrate" (and "demonstrating") as a verb whose subject is people or groups, in leadership or workplace text. It predicts a following quality noun such as commitment, dedication, respect or integrity.
result.label: verb "demonstrate" before virtue nouns
alloy 'loy' word piece
result.description: Fires on the 'loy' piece in 'alloy' and 'alloying' (al|loy), mostly in metallurgy and materials text. Upstream members are mainly 'loy' detectors across layers. It pushes towards suffixes like 'ed' and 'ing'.
